_about: The Consiliatio Cnuti in the translator’s order, assembled by tools/conscn/reading.py from the clause files (“beside”: printed by Liebermann beside the law it translates; “list”: printed in his list, Gesetze I pp. 618–619). “en” is an English crib: of the Latin itself (enOf “la”) or of the Old English source, from Liebermann’s German (enOf “oe”).

passages.text: Hic<ptr n="c" target="ConsCn_Inscr.lnote.oe.c"/> incipiunt leges Cnuti regis Anglorum, Danorum et Nororum<ptr n="d" target="ConsCn_Inscr.lnote.oe.d"/>, uiri iustissimi<ptr n="e" target="ConsCn_Inscr.lnote.oe.e"/><ptr n="e" target="ConsCn_Inscr.lnote.oe.e-2"/> et probatissimi.
passages.en: Here begin the laws of Cnut, king of the English, Danes and Norwegians, a most just and most approved man.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Inscr. roth Cb; den Anfang bis</hi> I 17 <hi rend="italic">lässt fort Hk, wo vorangeht</hi> ECf.
notes.en: Inscr. in red <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>; the beginning up to I 17 is omitted by <hi rend="italic">Hk</hi>, where ECf. precedes

notes.de: Dieses Lob ist vielleicht blosse Floskel; doch <hi rend="italic">s. Gl</hi> Cnut 5
notes.en: This praise is perhaps a mere flourish; but see <hi rend="italic">Gl</hi> Cnut 5

passages.text: Quoniam apud antiquos<ptr n="h" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.h"/>, ut auctoritate priorum didicimus, Anglia multorum regum fulta erat presidio, singulis<ptr n="1" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.1"/> regibus singulis regionibus presidentibus, diuersis etiam legalium consuetudinibus<ptr n="i" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.i"/><ptr n="i" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.i-2"/> utebantur, que quidem sub<ptr n="k" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.k"/><ptr n="k" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.k-2"/> paucitate uel unitate regiminis per diuersas regiones diuerse permanserunt — unde et plebeie consuetudines<ptr n="2" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.2"/> usque in hodiernum<ptr n="l" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.l"/><ptr n="l" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.l-2"/> diem permanserunt (<ptr n="3" target="ConsCn_Prooem-1.lnote.oe.3"/>indiscusse) et immutate perdurauerunt —.
passages.en: Since among the ancients, as we have learned from the authority of earlier men, England was supported by the protection of many kings, individual kings presiding over individual regions, they also used diverse customs of laws, which indeed, under a fewness or unity of rule, remained diverse throughout the diverse regions — whence also the customs of the common people have remained to this present day (undiscussed) and have endured unchanged —.

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">da die Dena lagu erst im</hi> 9. <hi rend="italic">Jh. anfing, meint Verf. ihre Verschiedenheit vom Westsachsen- und Mercier-Recht nicht oder doch nicht diese Dreitheilung allein</hi>
notes.en: since the Dena lagu began only in the 9th cent., the author does not mean its difference from West Saxon and Mercian law, or at any rate not this threefold division alone

notes.de: Dass jeder Kleinstaat vor Ecgberht eigenes Recht besass, ist wahrscheinlich richtig, aber vom Verf. schwerlich aus authentischen Quellen geschöpft
notes.en: That each petty kingdom before Ecgberht had its own law is probably correct, but the author can hardly have drawn this from authentic sources

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Verf. meint: von Ecgberht bis Cnut</hi>
notes.en: The author means: from Ecgberht to Cnut

notes.de: Dass nach Bildung von Gross-Mercien und Gross-Wessex <hi rend="italic">(paucitas)</hi> und vollends nach Ecgberht bis 1027 alles Recht ganz so vielgespalten blieb, wie im 5.—8. Jh., ist unrichtig
notes.en: That after the formation of Greater Mercia and Greater Wessex <hi rend="italic">(paucitas)</hi>, and still more after Ecgberht down to 1027, all law remained just as fragmented as in the 5th–8th cent., is incorrect

notes.de: Neben der Dreiteilung bestand eine viel mannigfachere Spaltung der Rechtsgewohnheit in den Niedergerichten um 1120. Letztere meint Verf. <hi rend="italic">Vgl. Gl</hi> Partikularrecht 13
notes.en: Alongside the threefold division there existed, around 1120, a far more varied fragmentation of legal custom in the lower courts. It is the latter that the author means. <hi rend="italic">Cf. Gl</hi> Partikularrecht 13

notes.de: perm. <hi rend="italic">ohne</hi> ind. <hi rend="italic">Cb;</hi> ind. <hi rend="italic">ohne</hi> perm. <hi rend="italic">Hr</hi>
notes.en: perm. without ind. Cb; ind. without perm. Hr

passages.text: Postquam autem Cnutum<ptr n="4" target="ConsCn_Prooem-2.lnote.oe.4"/> regem iustissimum<ptr n="m" target="ConsCn_Prooem-2.lnote.oe.m"/> totam Angliam obtinere contigit, rationabili consideratione decreuit, quatinus sicut uno rege, ita et una<ptr n="n" target="ConsCn_Prooem-2.lnote.oe.n"/> lege uniuersum Anglie regnum regeretur.
passages.en: But after it befell Cnut, the most just king, to obtain the whole of England, he decreed by reasonable consideration that, as by one king, so also by one law the whole kingdom of England should be ruled.

notes.de: Chn. <hi rend="italic">stets Hr; verb. aus</hi> Chutum <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>
notes.en: Chn. throughout Hr; corrected from Chutum Cb

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">übertrieben: vgl. II Cn</hi> 12. 14 <hi rend="italic">f.</hi> 71, 2 <hi rend="italic">f.</hi>
notes.en: exaggerated: cf. II Cn 12. 14 f. 71, 2 f.

passages.text: Conuocato itaque comitum procerumque<ptr n="o" target="ConsCn_Prooem-3.lnote.oe.o"/> necnon et cetere nobilitatis sapientieque totius Anglie concilio, satagebat communi decreto, ut, in quantum humana ratio ualuit, ea que iusta fuerant stabiliret, que autem in parte aberrauerant<ptr n="5" target="ConsCn_Prooem-3.lnote.oe.5"/> corrigeret, ea uero que omnino a rectitudinis tramite deuiauerant extirparet penitusque eradicaret.
passages.en: Having therefore called together a council of the earls and magnates and also of the rest of the nobility and wisdom of all England, he endeavoured by common decree, as far as human reason availed, to establish those things which had been just, to correct those which had partly gone astray, but to root out and utterly eradicate those which had wholly strayed from the path of rectitude.

passages.text: Quia uero omne ius ad Eum referendum est a quo omnis iustitia, quippe qui docet hominem scientiam<ptr n="p" target="ConsCn_Prooem-4.lnote.oe.p"/>, diuinaque humanis merito<ptr n="2" target="ConsCn_Prooem-4.lnote.oe.2"/> preponenda sunt, ecclesiastice uero<ptr n="6" target="ConsCn_Prooem-4.lnote.oe.6"/> institutiones<ptr n="q" target="ConsCn_Prooem-4.lnote.oe.q"/><ptr n="q" target="ConsCn_Prooem-4.lnote.oe.q-2"/> sinodorumque conuentus<ptr n="7" target="ConsCn_Prooem-4.lnote.oe.7"/> apud Anglos inusitati adhuc fuerant, ne quis ordo<ptr n="8" target="ConsCn_Prooem-4.lnote.oe.8"/> in regno suo titubaret, primum de ecclesiastico, deinde de seculari iure tractare incepit sic dicens<ptr n="9" target="ConsCn_Prooem-4.lnote.oe.9"/>:
passages.en: But since all law is to be referred to Him from whom is all justice, since he it is who teaches man knowledge, and divine things are rightly to be set before human ones, while ecclesiastical ordinances and the assemblies of synods had hitherto been unusual among the English, lest any order in his kingdom should totter, he began to treat first of ecclesiastical, then of secular law, speaking thus:

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">Ein Begriff:</hi> kanonisches Recht kraft [<hi rend="italic">rein geistlicher</hi>] Synoden; <hi rend="italic">letztere setzt Verf. als regelmässig schon seit Cnut an, betrachtet also die Reform nach etwa</hi> 1075 <hi rend="italic">nicht als neu</hi>
notes.en: A single concept: canon law by virtue of [purely ecclesiastical] synods; the author takes the latter to have been regular already from Cnut's time, and so does not regard the reform after about 1075 as new

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">schon seit Cnut</hi> streiche. Verf. schreibt (<hi rend="italic">s. o</hi>. S. 332₇), <hi rend="spaced">náchdem</hi> Reform des Kirchengerichts durch Wl ep und Synode seit Lanfranc etwas jahrelang Gewohntes, daher kirchliche Gesetzgebung durch den Staat veraltet und der Erklärung bedürftig geworden war. Von Lanfranc werden sechs Synoden gemeldet, die letzte liegt aber nur 15 Jahre hinter der ersten. Das ist kein so langer Zeitraum, wie ihn Verfasser zu meinen scheint. Wilhelm II. unterdrückte Anselms Neigung zu Synoden; erst 1102 konnte dieser wieder eine abhalten
notes.en: Delete <hi rend="italic">already from Cnut's time</hi>. The author is writing (<hi rend="italic">see above</hi> p. 332₇) <hi rend="italic">after</hi> the reform of the church courts by Wl ep and synods had, since Lanfranc, become something customary for years, so that legislation on church matters by the state had become obsolete and in need of explanation. Six synods are reported under Lanfranc, but the last lies only 15 years after the first. That is not so long a period as the author seems to think. William II suppressed Anselm's inclination to hold synods; only in 1102 was he able to hold one again

notes.de: Incipiunt decreta Cnuti regis <hi rend="italic">fügt roth ein Cb</hi>
notes.en: Incipiunt decreta Cnuti regis inserted in red by Cb

passages.text: Hec est consiliatio, quam Cnutus totius Anglie, Danorum et Nororum rex consiliatus est cum suis sapientibus apud Wintoniam, Deo ad laudem et sibimet ad regiam dignitatem et expeditionem; legat quilibet utram malit, siue secularem legem siue diuinam expeditionem.
passages.en: (Inscription. This is the ordinance which Cnut, king of all England and king of the Danes and king of the Norwegians, decreed, [he] and his witan, to the praise of God and to his own royal dignity and benefit; let each consider which of the two [to follow it or not] he will. A Cons.) (In the name of the Lord. This is the ordinance which the witan decided and devised after many good examples; and this was done as soon as King Cnut, with the counsel of his witan, had fully established peace and friendship between Danes and English and settled all their former disputes. D)

passages.text: Hec est consiliacio, quam Cnutus rex meditacionem suorum sapientum consiliatus est, Deo ad laudem et sibimet ad regiam dignitatem et expeditionem; hoc autem factum est in natali Domini apud Wintoniam.
passages.en: Prologue. This is the ordinance which King Cnut, king of all England and king of the Danes, decreed with the counsel of his witan, to the praise of God and to his own royal dignity and benefit (to the people, Ld Quadr.); and that was at the holy Christmas season at Winchester.

passages.text: Primum quidem, ut supra omnia unum Deum diligerent et honorarent et unam Christianitatem (diligenter) tenerent regemque suum recta fide amarent
passages.en: Namely, first, that above all other things they would always love and honour one God and unanimously hold one Christian faith, and love King Cnut with true loyalty. (D: 1. Now the first thing is that the witan decided that above all other things they would always honour one God and unanimously hold one Christian faith, and love King Cnut rightly and loyally, and eagerly follow Edgar's law. 1a. And they declared that they would further consider at leisure, with God's help, the people's needs as best they could. 1b. Now we will make clear what can be of benefit to us before God and the world; let whoever will pay heed. 1c. Let us very eagerly turn from sins and zealously atone for our misdeeds, and rightly love and honour one God and unanimously hold one Christian faith and eagerly shun all heathenism.)

passages.text: et Dei ecclesiam tutarentur, pacificarent et frequentarent.
passages.en: and let us protect and keep the peace of God's churches and visit them often, for the salvation of souls and for our own benefit.

passages.text: Omnis ecclesia est rite in Christi propria pace; et debet Christianus quisque scire, sibi in illa pace maximam reuerenciam deberi, quoniam pax Dei est omnium pacum optima promeritu et diligencia dignissima obseruatu, deinde regis.
passages.en: Every church is rightly under Christ's own protection; and every Christian man has great need to show great respect for that protection; for God's protection is of all protections the most to be earned and the most eagerly to be kept, and next to it the king's.

passages.text: Est ergo iustissimum, ut Dei ecclesie pax et Christiani regis manus pax stet semper inuiolata; et qui utram plene infregerit, careat terra et uita, nisi ei misericordiam rex prestare uoluerit.
passages.en: Now it is very right that the protection of God's church within its walls and the protection given by the Christian king's own hand stand equally (always, G) inviolate; and whoever wholly breaks either [by killing], let him lose land and life, unless the king is willing to pardon him.

passages.text: Et si posthac quisquam Dei ecclesie . . . ., homicida fiat, inemendabile habeatur; et persequatur eum omnis qui Dei sit amicus, nisi hoc fortasse contingat, quod evadens tam dignum locum adeat, quod ea causa rex ei uitam concedat pro plena satisfactione tam erga Deum quam erga homines.
passages.en: And if ever henceforth anyone so violates the protection of God's church that he becomes a manslayer within the church walls, then that is beyond compensation, and let everyone who is God's friend pursue him; unless it happens that he escapes from there and reaches so weighty a sanctuary that for its sake the king grants him his life, on full compensation both to God and to men:

passages.text: Que quidem primum est, ut sua redempcione se Deo et regi tradat; et inde se inleget ad emendacionem.
passages.en: and namely, first, that he pay his own wergild to Christ and to the king, and thereby buy himself back into the law so as to be allowed to make amends.

passages.text: Deinde enim debet ipsi ecclesie sue pacis infracturam secundum montam regis, templique purificacionem perquirat secundum illius dignitatem, emendetque tam cognacionis quam hominis emendam plenam, maximeque erga Deum.
passages.en: And if it then comes to compensation, the king permitting it, let [that] man pay compensation for [breach of] the church's protection to that [violated] church at the full [amount for] breach of the king's protection, and obtain the cleansing of the minster as is fitting, and pay compensation for the [slain man] in full, both as kinsman [to the kindred] and as dependant [to his lord], and above all make eager atonement to God.

passages.text: Si autem sine occisione pax ecclesie infracta fuerit, siue per pugnam siue per rapinam siue per malefactum, diligenter emendet iuxta modum ipsius malefacti:
passages.en: And if otherwise, [namely] where the [attacked] people stay alive, a church's protection is broken, let it be eagerly compensated according to what the deed is, whether by fighting or by robbery or by whatever it may be:

passages.text: primum autem ecclesie pacis infracturam iuxta modum ipsius malefacti et iuxta modum dignitatis ipsius ecclesie.
passages.en: let compensation first be paid to the [violated] church for the breach of protection, according to what the deed is and according to the rank of the church.

passages.text: Non enim omnes ecclesie eiusdem sunt dignitatis seculariter, licet diuinitus eandem habeant sanctificacionem.
passages.en: Not all churches are entitled to the same rank (of honour, G) in secular terms, although they have the same consecration (exorcism, G) in ecclesiastical terms.

passages.text: Matris ergo ecclesie pacis infracture emenda est iuxta montam regis, scilicet V libre in lege Anglorum; mediocris uero iuxta forisfacturam regis, uidelicet CXX solidi; agrestis autem ecclesie carentis cimiterio XXX solidi.
passages.en: Breach of the protection of a head minster in cases that can be compensated goes at [the amount of] the king's protection, that is with five pounds [of silver] under English law (and in Kent, for this breach of protection, five pounds [go] to the king and three to the archbishop, G); and of a middling minster with 120 shillings, that is at the king's fine; and of a still smaller one, where there is little divine service but there is a graveyard, with 60 shillings; and of a field-church, where there is no graveyard, with 30 shillings.

passages.text: Omnibus Christianis oportet rectissime, ut sacra et ordines et sanctificatas domos semper diligentissime pacificent et tutentur, ordinem unumquemque honorent secundum modum ipsius.
passages.en: It very rightly befits all Christian people always to protect and keep the peace of relics and men in orders and consecrated houses of God most eagerly, and to honour each order according to its rank.

passages.text: Quoniam, qui sciat intelligat, magnum esse et magnificum quod sacerdos habet ad faciendum populo ad necessitatem, si domino Deo suo acceptus erit in iustitia.
passages.en: For — let him understand who (will or, A) can — great and glorious is what a priest can do for the benefit of the people, if he pleases his Lord rightly:

passages.text: Magna enim est atque magnifica adiuracio, que demonia elongat et in fugam conuertit, quociens ipse baptizat uel eucaristiam sacrat, ubi eciam angeli circumuagantur accionemque custodiunt; per Dei uirtutem sacerdoti cooperantur, quociens ipse seruit Christo in iustitia.
passages.en: Great is the exorcism and glorious the consecration by which (he, A) drives out devils and puts them to flight, as often as baptism is given or the host consecrated (as he baptises someone or consecrates the host, A); and (holy, G) angels hover there (round about, G) and guard the [sacred] acts and through God's might help the priests, as often as they serve Christ rightly.

passages.text: Sic etiam faciunt, quociens ipsi diligenter et intimo corde Christum inuocant et pro populi necessitate interueniunt attente. Quapropter quisque debet per timorem Domini modum in ordine agnoscere cum discrecione.
passages.en: And so they always do, as often as they call eagerly to Christ from their inmost hearts and pray eagerly for the needs of the people; and therefore, for fear of God, one must recognise rank in holy orders with [clear] discernment.

passages.text: Si autem contigerit, ut sacerdos regulariter uiuens calumpnia et uicio causetur, et se innocentem nouerit, celebret missam, si audeat, et eucaristiam iam sumpturus ipse se ipsum super ipsam eucaristiam purget, si accusacio sit simplex;
passages.en: And if it happens that a priest who lives according to a rule is charged with an accusation and with evil practices, and he knows himself clean of it, let him say mass, if he dares, and clear himself (alone, G) by [taking] the sacrament, in the case of a simple accusation.

passages.text: si uero triplex, eodem modo cum aliis duobus sibi paribus ipse tertius se purget.
passages.en: And from a threefold accusation let him clear himself, if he dares, likewise by [taking] the sacrament, with two of his fellow-clergy.

passages.text: Quodsi diaconus regularis uite simplici causa accusatus fuerit, assumat duos suos pares et cum illis ipse tertius se purget;
passages.en: If a deacon who lives according to a rule is charged with a simple accusation, let him take two of his fellow-clergy and clear himself with them.

passages.text: si uero triplici, assumat VI et ipse sit septimus.
passages.en: And if he is charged with a threefold accusation, let him take six of his fellow-clergy and clear himself with them, and be himself the seventh [in the oath].

passages.text: Uulgaris autem presbiter, scilicet qui regularem uitam non ducit, si accusatus fuerit, purget se ut diaconus regularis.
passages.en: If a secular priest who does not live according to a rule is charged with an accusation, let him clear himself like a deacon who lives according to a rule.

passages.text: Si autem minister altaris accusatus adiutorio amicorum careat, offam iudicialem sumat et in ea diuinum iudicium subeat, nisi eucaristialem probacionem preeligat, et sibi liceat.
passages.en: If a servant of the altar who has no friends [or kin, and so] no oath-helpers is charged with an accusation, let him go to the [ordeal of the] consecrated morsel, and then experience [i.e. suffer] there what God wills, unless he is permitted to clear himself by [taking] the sacrament.

passages.text: Et si ordinatus mortis cause calumpniam patitur siue facti siue consilii, et se nocentem fuisse negauerit, purget se cognatis, quibus licet mortis causam simul cum eo aut ferre aut de mortis causa pro illo satisfacere.
passages.en: And if a cleric is charged with a feud and accused of having been a slayer by deed or by counsel, let him clear himself with his kinsmen, who must share the feud with him or pay compensation in his place.

passages.text: Si autem suffragio cognatorum careat, purget se sociis, aut ieiunium ineat et offam iudicialem sumat, et sic Dei iudicio probetur.
passages.en: And if he is without kin, let him clear himself with his fellows, or, if he must, begin a fast and go to the consecrated morsel, and experience [i.e. suffer] there as God may decree.

passages.text: Neque debet monasterii monacus satisfaccionem cause mortis humane uel soluere uel deprecari, quoniam ipse egreditur de lege cognacionis, cum regule legem subit.
passages.en: And no monk of a minster may anywhere lawfully demand feud-compensation [for the killing of his kinsman] or pay feud-compensation [for a killing by his kinsman]: he leaves his kin-law when he submits to the law of the rule.

passages.text: Si uero presbiter de falso testimonio uel periurio siue furto uel furti conscientia conuictus fuerit, ab ordinatorum consortio degradetur, careatque tam societate quam amicitia uniuersoque honore, nisi erga Deum et erga homines emendauerit, secundum quod episcopo uisum fuerit, fideiussoremque, se in posterum a tali crimine inmunem fore, dederit.
passages.en: And if a priest anywhere stands [convicted] of false witness or perjury, or is an accessory or accomplice of thieves, then let him be cast out of the fellowship of the clergy and lose both [their] fellowship and friendship and every honour, unless he makes all the deeper amends before God and men, as [his] bishop prescribes for him, and finds surety [to the effect] that he will forever desist from such [crimes].

passages.text: Uolumus etiam, ut omnis ordinis homines diligenter attendant, quisque ad hoc quod suum ordinem attinet.
passages.en: And we will (it is the ordinance of the witan that they will, D) that people of every order eagerly submit, each to the duty that belongs to him,

passages.text: Presertim ministri Domini, scilicet episcopi, abbates, monachi et monache ad rectitudinem sui ordinis se humilient et regulariter uiuant et die ac nocte sepe et frequenter inuocent Christum et pro uniuerso populo Christiano diligenter interueniant.
passages.en: and above all let the servants of God — bishops and abbots, monks and nuns [of a rule], canons and nuns — submit to their duty and live according to the rule, and by day and night often and frequently call to Christ and pray eagerly for all Christian people.

passages.text: Omnes namque Dei ministros precamur et monemus, et maxime sacerdotes, ut Deo obediant et castitatem diligant, semetipsos tuentes ab ira Dei [et] feruenti incendio quod feruet in inferno.
passages.en: And we ask and instruct all servants of God, and above all priests, to obey God and love chastity, and guard themselves against God's anger and against the surging fire that surges in hell.

passages.text: Satis enim certe sciunt, quod non debent recte communitatem mulieris secundum carnalem conuersacionem habere.
passages.en: They (we, D) know full well that they may not lawfully have intercourse with a woman.

passages.text: Quicumque ergo hinc occupatus, cessare et castitatem diligere uoluerit, Dei misericordiam consequatur et honorem seculi, sitque uirronis priuilegio dignus.
passages.en: And whoever will desist from this and keep chastity, let him have God's mercy, and as a worldly honour let him be entitled to a thegn's rights.

passages.text: Omnis etiam Christianus pro timore Domini iniustum coitum diligenter uitet et diuinam legem recte custodiat.
passages.en: And let every [other] Christian man also, for fear of his Lord, eagerly avoid unlawful intercourse and keep the law(s?) of God rightly.

passages.text: Docemus etiam et precamur ac in nomine Dei precipimus, ne quis Christianus infra sextum genu in sua cognacione uxorem ducat, neque alienam, cum qua cognatus suus supradicte propinquitatis carnaliter conuersatus est, neque cognatam illius, cum qua ipse rem habuit,
passages.en: And we instruct and (we, D) ask and command in God's name that no Christian man ever marry [a woman] of his own kin within the degree of [only] six persons, or the widow of his kinsman who was so closely related, or a blood-relative of the (his, A) wife whom he himself had before;

passages.text: [neque] illicitum coitum ambeat,
passages.en: nor let him commit fornication anywhere;

passages.text: neque amplius quam unam maritam habeat, eamque legaliter desponsatam, eaque sola [sit] contentus, dum illa uixerit, qui legem Dei recte obseruare uoluerit et ab inferni incendio animam tueri.
passages.en: nor let him have more wives than one, and that his betrothed wife; but (and, G) let whoever will rightly heed God's law and save his soul from hell-fire remain with the one as long as she lives.

passages.text: Statuimus etiam, ut rectitudines Dei quoquo anno soluantur:
passages.en: And let God's dues be paid lawfully and eagerly every year:

passages.text: que sunt aratri elemosina post XV dies post Pascha, iuuentutis decimacio ad Pentecosten, terre fructus ad festiuitatem Omnium sanctorum.
passages.en: namely plough-alms a fortnight after Easter, and the tithe of young stock at Pentecost, and [the tithe of] the fruits of the earth at All Saints [1 November].

passages.text: Si quis autem hanc decimacionem, sicut prediximus, soluere repugnauerit (ea est decimum iugum, sicut arauerit), adeat prepositus regis cum preposito episcopi et preposito ipsius domini terre, necnon [presbiter] ipsius ecclesie, ad quam decimacio attinet; qui inuito decimam illam auferant ecclesieque reddant et nonam partem tantum illi dimittant; octoque partes equaliter diuidant, quarum altera quidem domino, altera uero contingat episcopo, cuiuscumque homo ipse sit, siue episcopi siue regis siue uirronis.
passages.en: And if anyone then refuses to pay the tithe as we have ordained — namely [every] tenth acre, as the plough passes over it —, then let the king's reeve and the bishop's [reeve] and the [reeve] of the lord of the immunity and the priest of the [entitled] minster go [to him], and take the tenth part against his will for the minster to which it belongs, and assign him the ninth part; and let the [remaining] eight parts be divided in two, and let the landlord take half, the bishop half, whether [the refuser] is the king's man or a thegn's.

passages.text: Et Rome census soluatur ad festum sancti Petri;
passages.en: And Rome-money at St Peter's day (1 August, Quadr., Inst.);

passages.text: et quicumque illum ultra prenominatum diem tenuerit, reddat episcopo ipsum denarium et insuper [XXX] et regi CXX solidos.
passages.en: and whoever withholds it beyond that day, let him give the bishop the penny and 30 (pence, A) besides, and the king 120 (220, A) shillings.

passages.text: Et ecclesiasticus census ad festum sancti Martini.
passages.en: And church-scot at Martinmas [11 November].

passages.text: Et quicumque illum ulterius . ., reddat illum episcopo, persoluatque illum undecies, et regi CXX solidos.
passages.en: And whoever withholds it beyond that day, let him pay it to the bishop and pay it [to him] elevenfold, and the king 120 (220, A) shillings.

passages.text: Si quis autem uirronum in sua libera terra ecclesiam habeat, tertiam partem proprie decime det sue ecclesie.
passages.en: If, however, it is one of the thegns who has on his bookland a church at which there is a graveyard, let him pay a third of the tithe [owed] by him to [this] his church.

passages.text: Si uero cimiterium desit, de nona parte det presbitero quantum sibi libuerit.
passages.en: (And, G) if anyone has an [estate-]church at which there is no graveyard, let him give his priest what he will from the nine [remaining] parts.

passages.text: Omnisque census ecclesiasticus contingat monasterio ueteri secundum unumquemque liberum focum.
passages.en: And let every church-scot from every free hearth go to the old minster.

passages.text: Et census luminaris ter in anno: primum in uigilia Pasche obolata cere ab omni hida et iterum in festiuitate Omnium sanctorum tantumdem et tertio in Purificacione sancte Marie tantumdem.
passages.en: And light-dues three times a year: half a penny's worth of wax from every hide, first on Easter Eve and again at (before, A) All Saints [1 November] as much (and again at the Purification of Mary [eve of 2 February] as much, Ld and the Latin versions).

passages.text: Et anime simbola soluatur adhuc aperto sepulcro.
passages.en: And as for soul-scot, it is most right that it always be paid at once at the open grave.

passages.text: Et si quis funus aliquod extra parochiam illius deferri fecerit, soluat tamen anime simbolam ecclesie, ad quam illud attinet.
passages.en: And if any body is buried elsewhere, outside its proper confessional district, let the soul-scot nevertheless be paid to the minster to which it belonged.

passages.text: Et omnes rectitudines Dei conseruentur, sicut expedit.
passages.en: And let all God's dues be eagerly promoted (protected, A), as is needful.

passages.text: Et festa et ieiunia recte obseruentur.
passages.en: And let feasts and fasts be kept lawfully.

passages.text: Dieique Dominice uacacio teneatur a nona Sabbati usque ad diluculum diei Lune, sic et omnis festi, sicut indictum est.
passages.en: And let the festival of every Sunday be kept from Saturday noon until Monday dawn, and every other mass-day, as it is commanded.

passages.text: Interdicimus etiam diligenter diei Dominice mercacionem et omnem uulgi placitacionem, nisi necessitas arta coegerit,
passages.en: And trading on Sundays (on Sunday, B) we also strictly forbid, and every public assembly [for justice], unless it is for great necessity.

passages.text: [15, 1] et omnem uenacionem et omnem secularem operacionem.
passages.en: And let hunting and all worldly work be eagerly given up on that holy day.

passages.text: [16] Edicimus etiam, ut omne indictum ieiunium siue quadragesimale siue legitimum siue uigiliarum, id est omnis festi apostolorum, preter festum Philippi et Iacobi, quod precedente ieiunio Resurrectionis gratia caret, siue omnis diei Ueneris, nisi festum sit, summopere conseruetur.
passages.en: (Of fasting, B) And that every commanded fast be kept with all eagerness, whether it be an Ember fast or a Lenten fast or any other fast.

passages.text: [16, 1] A Pascha tamen usque ad Pentecosten non oportet ieiunium obseruare, nisi penitencie satisfactione uel ultro ieiunare uelit; sic et a natali Domini usque ad octauam Teophanie.
passages.en: And there is no need to fast from Easter until Pentecost — unless someone has been given penance or otherwise [voluntarily] wishes to fast — and (likewise, G) from midwinter until the octave of Epiphany (that is, seven days after Twelfth Day [6 January], G).

passages.text: [17] Interdicimus etiam iudicialem probacionem et iuraiuranda festis et constitutis ieiuniis et ab Aduentu Domini usque ad octauam Epiphanie et a Septuagesima usque ad quintam decimam diem post diem Dominice resurrectionis.
passages.en: And we forbid ordeals and [judicial] oaths on feast-days and Ember days and Lenten days and days of lawful fasting, and from Advent until the eighth day [13 January] after Twelfth Day has passed, and from Septuagesima until a fortnight after Easter.

passages.text: Et festum sancti Edwardi sapientes instituerunt seruari per totam Angliam XV. kalendas Aprilis, necnon et sancti Dunstani XIIII. kal. Iunii.
passages.en: And the witan have chosen that the feast of St Edward is to be celebrated throughout all England on 18 March (namely on the 14th, wrongly, G), and the feast of St Dunstan on 19 May (that is, on 13 May, wrongly, G).

passages.text: Sitque in sanctis temporibus omnibus Christianis, ueluti iustissimum est, pax et concordia communis omnisque inimicitia segregata.
passages.en: And at the holy seasons, as is right, let there be peace and concord among all Christian people, and every lawsuit (fraud, Ld) suspended.

passages.text: Et si quis cuiquam debet fideiussionem uel solucionem de seculari negotio, soluat illi uel cito uel sero.
passages.en: And if anyone owes another a loan or compensation in secular matters, let him pay it to him willingly before or after [the feast],

passages.text: Postulamus etiam pro Dei amore, ut quisque Christianus diligenter attendat ad suam propriam utilitatem,
passages.en: (We wish, B) and we ask for the love of God that every Christian man earnestly understand his own good:

passages.text: quoniam omnis nostrum unum tempus uidebit, quando magis diligeret uoluntatem Dei fecisse quam [quidquid] in mundo habetur.
passages.en: For we shall all live to see a time when it would be dearer to us than everything on earth that (before? had there, G) we had eagerly (always, G) done God's will while we could.

passages.text: Sed nobis debebitur retribucio, secundum quod promeremur, dum uiuimus; ue tunc illi qui ante promeruit supplicium inferni!
passages.en: But then we shall have a single reward for what we did before in life; woe then to him who has earned hell-torment!

passages.text: Diligenter ergo ab iniquitate recedamus confessoribusque nostris peccata nostra confiteamur et deinceps cessemus et perpetrata corrigamus.
passages.en: (Of confession. B) But let us very eagerly turn from sins, and let each of us eagerly confess his misdeeds to our confessors, and ever desist from them and eagerly make amends.

passages.text: Faciamusque unusquisque alii quod sibi uellet ab eo fieri: hoc est iustum iudicium et Deo acceptissimum; felix qui hoc iudicium obseruauerit,
passages.en: And let each of us offer the other what we wish to be offered to us: that is a just principle and most pleasing to God; and he will be most blessed who keeps that principle.

passages.text: quoniam Deus omnipotens nos omnes creauit et iterum caro precio redemit, id est propria uita, quam ille pro nobis tribuit.
passages.en: For God Almighty created us all and afterwards bought us at a high price (prices, A), namely with his own life (blood, B), which he gave (shed, B) for us all.

passages.text: Itaque omnis Christianus quod sibi expediat faciat: Christianitatem suam diligenter custodiat, ad eucaristie percepcionem saltim ter in anno se ipsum preparet, quicumque propriam utilitatem, ueluti sibi expedit, considerare uoluerit.
passages.en: But let every Christian man do what he needs to: take (ever, A) eager care of his Christianity, and let each who will understand his own good prepare himself to go to communion at least three times a year, as he needs to.

passages.text: Et uerba et opera omnis amicus moderetur recte, iusiurandum et manufirmacionem caute obseruet,
passages.en: And let each of [our] friends order word and work rightly and carefully keep oath and pledge.

passages.text: et omnem iniusticiam, in quantum quis poterit, ab hac patria eiciat;
passages.en: And let every injustice be eagerly cast out of this country, as far as it can be done;

passages.text: Deique iusticiam amodo diligat tam in uerbo quam in opere; sic enim omnis Dei misericordiam assequetur.
passages.en: and let [people] (lacking in G) eagerly love God's law henceforth in word and deed: then God's mercy will be all the readier for us all.

passages.text: Faciamus igitur quod adhuc docere uolumus: simus domino nostro semper fidi et fideles et totis uiribus nostris honorem eius sustineamus et uoluntatem eius impleamus.
passages.en: Let us also act eagerly, as we will now further instruct: let us always be loyal and faithful to our lord, and ever with all our might exalt his honour and do his will.

passages.text: Quidcunque enim pro iusta dileccione domini facimus, totum nobismet ipsis ad magnam utilitatem facimus. (Illum namque Deus diligit, qui suum dominum recta fide diligit.) Illi namque Deus est fidus, qui suo domino recte est fidus.
passages.en: For all that we ever do out of true loyalty to our lord, we do it all to our own great benefit; for God will certainly be gracious to him who is rightly loyal to his lord.

passages.text: Sic et dominum quemque suos homines recte seruare oportet.
passages.en: And also every lord has very great need to treat his men rightly.

passages.text: Docemus etiam omnes Christianos, ut intimo corde semper Deum diligant et rectam Christianitatem diligenter teneant et diuinis doctoribus sollicite obediant Deique doctrinam et legem satagant scire et inuestigent sepe et frequenter, sibimet ipsis ad utilitatem.
passages.en: And we very earnestly instruct all Christian people always to love God from their inmost hearts and eagerly hold true Christianity and eagerly obey their spiritual teachers, and often and diligently consider and study God's teachings and laws, for their own benefit.

passages.text: Hortamur quoque, ut omnis Christianus discat, quatinus nouerit saltem ueram fidem semper intelligere recte et Dominicam oracionem et catholicam fidem discat,
passages.en: And we instruct that every Christian man learn [so much] that he can at least rightly understand the true faith, and learn the Pater noster and the Creed.

passages.text: quoniam altera quidem cum domino Deo loquimur, altera uero rectam fidem indicamus.
passages.en: For with the first every Christian man is to pray to God, and with the second declare the true faith.

passages.text: Ipse enim dominus Ihesus Christus primus illam oracionem orauit suisque discipulis insinuauit.
passages.en: Christ himself first sang the Pater noster and taught that prayer to his disciples.

passages.text: In qua Dominica oracione continentur VII preces; quibus qui attento animo orauerit, seruiet legacionem ad Deum, pro qualibet necessitate facit, tam presentis uite quam future.
passages.en: And in that divine prayer there are seven petitions; with them, whoever sings it inwardly intercedes with God himself for every need that one has, either for this life or for the life to come.

passages.text: Quomodo poterit quisquam intime pro se Deum orare, qui erga Deum rectam fidem non habet?
passages.en: But how can anyone ever pray inwardly to God unless he has inwardly (true love and, G) true faith in God?

passages.text: Neque illi debetur post obitum Christianorum communio in sanctificata requie, uel in hac uita est dignus eucaristia.
passages.en: For after his death he may not rest in consecrated ground with the (Christian, A) community of Christians (he has neither fellowship with Christian people nor [the right] to rest in consecrated ground, G), or here in life be worthy of the sacrament (nor may he receive the holy sacrament, G).

passages.text: Quinimmo non bene Christianus est, qui hec di[s]cere neglexerit; nec debet rite alium ad fontem baptismatis suscipere neque ad manus impositionem episcopi uenire, donec ea bene didiscerit.
passages.en: Nor (Therefore, A) is he truly a Christian who will (would, A) not learn it, nor may he lawfully receive anyone [as godparent] at baptism, or any more from the bishop's hand [as sponsor at confirmation], before he learns it so that he knows it well.

passages.text: Adhuc ortamur, ut criminalia peccata et diabolica facta quisque a se arceat in omni tempore; et diligentissime emendet secundum sui confessoris . . ., quisquis per impulsum diaboli in peccatum corruit.
passages.en: (Good teaching, B) And we instruct that people guard themselves very eagerly at all times against grievous sins (sin, B) and devilish deeds; and let whoever falls into sins at the devil's prompting atone very eagerly according to his confessor's advice.

passages.text: Docemus quoque, ut ab incesta lasciuia et iniusta uenere, necnon et qualibet legis transgressione prudenter sibi caueat.
passages.en: And we instruct that people always (eagerly, B) beware of foul lust and unlawful intercourse and every kind of adultery.

passages.text: Monemusque hominem quemque, ut timorem Dei iugiter in memoria habeat dieque noctuque propter peccata sua diem iudicii metuat, inferni orrorem formidet, uiteque sue diem nouissimum prope esse existimet.
passages.en: And we also earnestly instruct everyone to have the fear of God always in mind, and by day and night to be afraid of sins, to dread Judgment Day and shudder at hell, and always to expect his last day to be near.

passages.text: Episcopi sunt precones Dei et diuine legis doctores; hii debent cum summa diligencia predicare et exemplificare spirituale proficuum, obseruet qui uelit.
passages.en: Bishops are heralds and teachers of God's law (God's teachers, B), and they must preach and eagerly show by example what is spiritually needful; let him heed it who will.

passages.text: Debilis namque nimium custos ipse ad custodiam inuentus est, qui custodiam cui preest saltim ex preclamacione defendere non uult, nisi aliter queat, si quis latro latrocinari incipit.
passages.en: For that shepherd is found weak for his flock who will not defend the flock which he must keep — if he cannot do it in some other [stronger] way — by shouting, if any public enemy [the arch-enemy] begins to do harm there.

passages.text: Set nullus latro tam nocens ut diabolus, qui semper circa hoc satagit, qualiter in animabus hominum maxime latrocinari possit.
passages.en: There is no robber so evil as the devil himself: he is always intent on one thing, how he can do most harm among men's souls (to men in their souls, B A).

passages.text: Oportet itaque custodes esse peruigiles diligenterque uociferantes, qui aduersus puplicum latronem populum protegere debent: hii sunt episcopi et presbiteri, qui diuinam custodiam patrocinari tutarique debent sapientibus doctrinis, ne forte ille dementer auidus uirlupus supra modum a diuina custodia dirripiat et mortificet.
passages.en: Then the shepherds who must shield the people against the public enemy must be very watchful and eagerly cry out: namely the bishops and priests, who must guard and defend the spiritual flock with wise teaching, so that the madly greedy werewolf does not tear too much, nor devour too many of the spiritual flock.

passages.text: Quicumque autem [de]dignabitur Dei nuncio obaudire, habeat hoc commune cum ipso Deo!
passages.en: And whoever scorns to listen to God's messengers, let him settle that with God himself!

passages.text: Sit nomen Dei semper benedictum, cui laus, gloria et honor in eterna secula! Amen.
passages.en: (Epilogue. May God's name be blessed eternally for ever, and praise and glory and honour to him always, for ever and ever! Amen. B, Consiliatio)

passages.text: [<hi rend="italic">Prol</hi>.] De lege seculari. Hec est autem secularis conciliacio, quam ego uolo cum meis sapientibus consiliari super uniuersam Angliam.
passages.en: Prologue. This, then, is the secular ordinance which I will, with the counsel of my witan, that men keep throughout all England.

passages.text: [1] Primum quidem est, quod uolo, ut recta lex erigatur, et omnis iniuria deiciatur, et omnis iniusticia emundetur et eradicetur, in quantum humana ratio et diligentia ualeat, ab hac patria, Deique rectitudo erigatur.
passages.en: Namely, first, that I will (And it is the decision of the witan, D) that just laws be set up and every unjust law eagerly suppressed, and that every injustice be weeded out and rooted up from this country as eagerly as possible, and God's law be raised up,

passages.text: [1, 1] Amodo paciamur hominem quemque, miserum tam quam felicem, puplica rectitudine dignum esse, et ut illi iustum iudicium iudicetur.
passages.en: and that henceforth every person, poor as well as rich, be allowed (to be, D) entitled to folk-right, and just judgments be given him.

passages.text: [2] Et docemus, quamuis quis peccet et se ipsum profunde forisfaciat, [tunc] correctio moderetur, ita quod propter Deum sit parcibilis et propter seculum sustentibilis.
passages.en: And we instruct (it is the decision of the witan, D) that, even if someone sins and forfeits himself deeply, the punishment be so ordered (moderated, D) as can be justified before God and tolerated in the world.

passages.text: [2<hi rend="italic">a</hi>] Quicunque ergo iudicii potestatem habeat, diligenter memoretur, quod ipse petat, dum dicit: ‘Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus!’
passages.en: And let whoever has the power of judgment consider very earnestly what he himself desires (from us, D) when he says: ‘And forgive us our debts, as we forgive’ (that is in English: ‘and forgive us, Lord, our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us’, G).

passages.text: [2, 1] Interdicimus, ne quis quemquam pro modico admisso morte condempnet, set pocius discernatur pacifica correctio populo ad commodum, neque pro modico manuum Dei creatura eiusque proprius mercatus, quem care emit, deterreatur.
passages.en: And we command (forbid, B; it is the decision of the witan, D) that Christian people are at least not to be condemned to death for all too small [offences]; but let [life-]sparing punishments be decided on instead, for the benefit of the people, and let God's handiwork and his own property, which he bought dearly (deeply, A), not be destroyed for small [offences].

passages.text: [3] Interdicimus etiam, ne Christiani foras a patria uenundentur, presertim in paganism[um] non tradantur; sed diligenter parcatur animabus, quas Christus propria uita comparauit.
passages.en: And we command (forbid, A; it is the decision of the witan, D) that Christian people are not to be sold out of the country all too readily, at least not brought into heathendom; but let people take great care not to destroy those souls (that soul, G) which Christ bought with his own life.

passages.text: [4] Edicimus quoque, ut patriam in finibus omnibus mundemus, et ut a sceleribus cessetur.
passages.en: And we command (it is the decision of the witan, D) that the land be eagerly cleansed in every part, and that wicked deeds cease everywhere.

passages.text: [4<hi rend="italic">a</hi>] Quodsi uenefici aut magi uel latrones-homicide siue meretrices usquam reperiantur, euentilentur a patria aut in patria pereant, nisi cessent et de patratis satisfaciant.
passages.en: (Witches. B) And if witches or soothsayers, secret murderers or whores are found anywhere in the land, let them be eagerly driven out of this country, or destroyed (let them perish, G) utterly in the land, unless they desist [from evil] and atone all the more deeply.

passages.text: [4, 1] Edicimus etiam, ut discoli et exleges Dei et hominum a patria discedant, nisi se dedant et emendent.
passages.en: And we command (it is the decision of the witan, D) that apostates and outlaws of God and men depart from the land, unless they submit and atone all the more eagerly.

passages.text: Fures et latrones sine dilacione pereant, nisi tempore cessent.
passages.en: And let thieves and public robbers perish forthwith, unless they desist [from evil].

passages.text: Interdicimus quoque omnem paganissimum.
passages.en: (Of heathenism. B) And we strictly forbid all heathenism.

passages.text: Paganissimus quippe est, ut quis idola colat, scilicet paganos deos, solem et lunam, ignem uel flumen, fontes et saxa siue cuiusquam generis arborem aut ueneficium diligat seu homicidium furtiuum efficiat ullo modo siue in sanguine uel in transmigracione uel in talibus erroribus quicquam factitet.
passages.en: Heathenism (That, B) is, that one worships idols, namely that one worships heathen gods and the sun or moon, fire or flood, springs or stones or forest trees of any kind, or practises witchcraft, or commits secret murder in any way, either by sacrifice (by casting lots, A) or (by, B) divination, or carries out anything of such delusions.

passages.text: Homicide, periuri, ordinis infractores et legis transgressores recedant et satisfaciant, aut a patria cum peccato discedant.
passages.en: Let manslayers and perjurers, violators of holy orders and adulterers submit and make amends, or depart from their homeland with their sins (sin, D).

passages.text: Parasiti, mentitores, raptores, dispoliatores Dei odio habeantur, nisi cessauerint et plene satisfecerint.
passages.en: Hypocrites (lickers? A) and liars, robbers and plunderers shall have God's anger, unless they desist [from evil] and atone all the more deeply.

passages.text: Et qui patriam recte emundare iniusticiamque deicere, iusticiam autem diligere uoluerit, illum oportet diligenter talia abhorrere et corrigere.
passages.en: And whoever wishes to cleanse the land rightly and put down injustice (ever, A?) and love righteousness (the righteous, A?), then he must eagerly restrain such things and shun such things.

passages.text: Attendamus etiam circa quietudinis emendam et circa census emendam: sic quidem circa quietudinis emendam, ut possessori sit commodissimum, furi uero incommodissimum; sic uero circa census emendam, ut per totam gentem una moneta eat omni falsitate carens et quam nemo repudiet.
passages.en: (Reform of the coinage. B) Let us also all very earnestly consider the improvement of public security and (lacking in G) the improvement of the coinage: on public security, in the way that is best for the householder (the farmer) and most hateful to thieves; and on reform of the coinage, that one coinage be current throughout all this nation without any falseness; and let no one refuse it.

passages.text: Quisquis autem posthac falsum fabricauerit, amittat manum, qua illud falsum fabricauit, neque illam quacunque re, siue auro siue argento, redimat.
passages.en: And whoever makes false coin after this, let him lose the hand with which he made the false coin; and let him not buy it back on any terms, neither with gold nor with silver.

passages.text: Quod si monetarius prepositum accusauerit, quod illius licencia falsum fabricauerit, purget se triplici purgamine; quod si defecerit, idem iudicium sustineat quod ipse qui illud falsum fabricauit.
passages.en: And if the reeve is then accused of the false coin having been made with his permission, let him clear himself with the threefold clearing; and if the clearing then fails, let him receive the same judgment as he who made the false coin.

passages.text: Mensuras et pondera diligenter dirigamus et ab omni iniusto cessemus.
passages.en: And let measures and weights be carefully corrected, and let every injustice cease henceforth.

passages.text: Urbium refectiones, nauium profectus incipiamus et proficiamus, cum necesse sit pro communi utilitate.
passages.en: And let the repair of fortresses and the repair of bridges and the equipping of ships be eagerly undertaken, and military service likewise, whenever there is need for the common good.

passages.text: Meditemur etiam semper omni modo, qualiter primum possimus concilium consulere genti ad utilitatem et rectam Christianitatem maxime exaltare omnemque iniusticiam deicere.
passages.en: And let people always (eagerly, B) consider in every way how they can first devise a beneficial plan for the good of the people, and most highly exalt true Christianity, and most (eagerly, B) abolish every abuse of law.

passages.text: Propter hoc enim in patria prosperabitur ad opulenciam, si iniusticiam deiecerimus et iusticiam amauerimus pro Deo et seculo. Amen!
passages.en: For things will become considerably better in the land through putting down injustice and loving righteousness in matters spiritual and secular. Amen.

passages.text: De iure domini regis. Hee sunt rectitudines, quas rex habet super omnes homines in Westsexia; que sunt: monte fractura, domi inuasio, obstitus, exercitus reatus, nisi cui rex misereri uoluerit.
passages.en: These are the [jurisdictional] rights which the king has [reserved] over all men in Wessex: namely breach of [his special] protection, and [unlawful] attack on a house, obstruction (and harbouring outlaws, G), and the fine for [neglect of] military service, unless he wishes to honour someone further (by granting him the jurisdiction [over these too], G).

passages.text: Et si quis exlegis factum fecerit, consideret rex de pace.
passages.en: (Outlaw. B) And whoever commits a deed that incurs outlawry: let the king decide on his [being restored to the] peace.

passages.text: Si autem liberam terram habeat, sit forisfacta in manu regis, cuiuscunque homo sit.
passages.en: And if he has bookland, let it be forfeited into the king's hand, whosever man he may be.

passages.text: Quicunque etiam illum exlegem pauerit uel procurauerit, soluat V libras regi, nisi iurauerit, quod illum exlegem esse nesciuit.
passages.en: And whoever feeds or harbours that outlaw, let him pay the king 5 pounds, unless he clears himself [by showing] that he did not know him to be outlawed.

passages.text: Et in lege Merce habet super omnes homines, ut prescriptum est.
passages.en: And in Mercia he [the king] has [the rights] over all men, as is written above.

passages.text: Et in lege Danorum habet pugne reatum, pacis fracturam et domi inuasionem, nisi quid remissionis impendere uoluerit.
passages.en: And in the Danelaw he [the king] has [reserved] the fine for fighting (false coining, Inst.) and the fine for [neglect of] military service, breach of [the king's] protection and [unlawful] attack on a house, unless he wishes to honour someone further [by granting jurisdiction over these crimes too].

passages.text: Et si quis exlegem seruauerit uel procurauerit, satisfaciat, ut supra dictum est.
passages.en: And if anyone keeps the (then an, B A?) outlawed man [under protection] or harbours (an outlaw, G), let him pay compensation for it as was the law before.

passages.text: Quicunque aut iniusticiam statuerit aut iniustum iudicium amodo iudicauerit siue propter odium siue propter munus, sit reus aduersus regem CXX solid. secundum legem Anglorum, nisi iuramento asserere audeat, se rectius discernere nescisse; dignitate sua tamen omni tempore careat, nisi illam a rege iuxta eius libitum redimere ualuerit.
passages.en: And whoever henceforth sets up an unjust law (laws, D?) or gives a false judgment out of hatred or for (lacking in A D) a bribe, let him be liable to the king for 120 shillings (his wergild, A) under English law — unless he dares to declare on oath that he did not know how to do it more justly — and lose his thegnly rank [with his jurisdiction] for ever, unless he buys it back (again, G) from the king, as the king is willing to permit him.

passages.text: Quisquis uero iustam legem et iustum iudicium recusauerit, reus sit erga illum qui presidet, siue erga regem CXX sol., siue erga comitem XL solidorum, siue erga centenarium XXX sol. in lege Anglorum, siue quemque eorum, si sic contigerit.
passages.en: And whoever refuses [to obey] just law and right judgment, let him be liable to the one to whom it belongs [to receive the fine for disobeying the court]: either to the king 120 shillings, or to the earl 60 (40, D Cons.) shillings, or to the hundred 30 (20, B) shillings, or to each of them, if it so happens, under English law.

passages.text: In lege uero Danorum quisquis iustam legem detererit, soluat legis fracturam.
passages.en: And whoever in the Danelaw violates just law (laws, D?), let him pay lahslit.

passages.text: Et qui alium de iniquitate accusare uoluerit, quod ipse utro aut censu aut commodo deterior sit, si tunc alius id quod sibi imponitur falsificare quiuerit, sit ipse reus lingue, nisi illam proprie redempcionis censu redemerit.
passages.en: And whoever wishes to accuse another maliciously, so that the latter is harmed thereby either in property or in prosperity (life, Ld Inst.; maintenance? A): if the other [accused] can then prove false what he wished to charge him with, let him be liable [to lose] his tongue, unless he redeems himself with his wergild.

passages.text: Neque adeat quisquis regem, nisi nequeat rectum habere in suo centenario.
passages.en: And let no one apply to the king, unless he cannot obtain [his] rights within his hundred.

passages.text: Centenariique conuentus adeatur super forefacturam, secundum quod rectum est aditu.
passages.en: (Let one attend one's hundred. B) And let the hundred-court be attended on pain of a fine, as it is right (lacking in G) to attend it.

passages.text: Et conuentus urbis ter in anno et bis conuentus comitatus aut sepius.
passages.en: And let the borough-court be held three times a year and the shire-court twice (two, B A), unless it is (needed, B; Quadr. II; Inst.) more often.

passages.text: In illo autem conuentu comitatus assint episcopus et preses, ibique doceant tam Dei quam seculi iusticiam.
passages.en: And let the bishop of the shire and the ealdorman be present there, and let them both direct there both God's law and secular law.

passages.text: extra comitatum, nisi primum ter postulauerit suum rectum in suo centenario. Neque capiat quisquam captionem neque intra comitatum neque
passages.en: (Of distraint. B) And let no one take a distress [from his opponent to enforce a judgment], either within the shire[-court] or outside the shire, until he has three times asked for his right [in vain] in the hundred[-court].

passages.text: Ubi tercio si iusticia sibi defecerit, quarto petat comitatus conuentum, qui ei quartum terminum ponat.
passages.en: If he obtains no right the third time, then [only] let him go the fourth time to the shire-court; and let the shire set him (then, A) the fourth term.

passages.text: Qui si defecerit, accipiat licentiam utrimque et hinc et inde suum (ius) perquirendi.
passages.en: But if that fails, then let him take permission, from here and there [i.e. from both courts], to seize [in self-help] for his own property.

passages.text: [Teoþunga<ptr n="r" target="ConsCn_II-19-2a.lnote.oe.r"/><ptr n="11" target="ConsCn_II-19-2a.lnote.oe.11"/><ptr n="r" target="ConsCn_II-19-2a.lnote.oe.r-2"/>. Sicut regnum diuiditur in plures comitatus, comitatus in plura centenaria, ita centenarium unum in plures decimationes, sicut centum unum in plures decarios<ptr n="12" target="ConsCn_II-19-2a.lnote.oe.12"/> numeros.
passages.en: [<hi rend="italic">Teoþunga</hi> (tithings). As the kingdom is divided into several shires, the shire into several hundreds, so one hundred is divided into several tithings, as the number one hundred into several tens.

notes.de: 19, 2<hi rend="italic">a—d nur in Hk, verfasst im</hi> 12. <hi rend="italic">Jh., vielleicht in Kent und</hi> (<hi rend="italic">laut Sprachgebrauchs:</hi> centenarium, decimatio) <hi rend="italic">wohl vom Autor der Consil., aber, da</hi> Hr <hi rend="italic">fehlend, erst nachträglich. Vgl. über diese Glosse Palgrave</hi> Rise II <hi rend="italic">p.</hi> cxxv; <hi rend="italic">Waitz</hi> Deutsche Verf. I 448
notes.en: 19, 2a—d only in Hk, composed in the 12th cent., perhaps in Kent and (to judge by the usage: centenarium, decimatio) probably by the author of the Consil., but, since missing in Hr, only subsequently. On this gloss cf. Palgrave Rise II p. cxxv; Waitz Deutsche Verf. I 448

passages.text: Decimatio autem continet uel X uel<ptr n="13" target="ConsCn_II-19-2b.lnote.oe.13"/> XX uel XXX homines secundum loci consuetudinem.
passages.en: A tithing, moreover, contains either ten or twenty or thirty men, according to the custom of the place.

notes.de: l'XX, l'XXX <hi rend="italic">Hk, daher früher</hi> 70, 80 <hi rend="italic">missverstanden</hi>
notes.en: l'XX, l'XXX Hk, hence formerly misunderstood as 70, 80

passages.text: Qui omnes debent esse fideiussores singulorum, ita ut, si quis de illis calumpniam patitur, ceteri illum producant ad iusticiam; et si negat, purgationem legalem debet habere: ex sua propria decimatione secum iuraturos assumet.
passages.en: All of whom must be sureties for each one, so that, if any of them suffers an accusation, the others shall bring him to justice; and if he denies it, he must have lawful purgation: he shall take those who are to swear with him from his own tithing.

passages.text: Decimatio autem est que alicubi dicitur uulgo warda<ptr n="s" target="ConsCn_II-19-2d.lnote.oe.s"/><ptr n="s" target="ConsCn_II-19-2d.lnote.oe.s-2"/> — id est obseruatio: scilicet sub una societate urbem uel centenarium<ptr n="14" target="ConsCn_II-19-2d.lnote.oe.14"/> debet seruare —, alicubi<ptr n="t" target="ConsCn_II-19-2d.lnote.oe.t"/> dicitur borch — id est fideiussor<ptr n="a" target="ConsCn_II-19-2d.lnote.oe.a"/>, propter superius dictam causam, scilicet fideiussionem communem —, alicubi uero decimatio, quia X ad minus debent inesse.]
passages.en: A tithing, moreover, is what in some places is commonly called <hi rend="italic">warda</hi> — that is, watch: namely, under one fellowship it must guard the town or the hundred —, in some places is called <hi rend="italic">borch</hi> — that is, surety, for the reason stated above, namely common suretyship —, but in some places tithing, because at least ten must be in it.]
