passages.text: Uolumus etiam, ut omnis liber sit in centenario et in decimacione positus (quicunque dignus esse uoluerit purgacione aut redempcione, si quis eum peremerit), supra duodecim annos; aut nulla libertatis rectitudine dignus habeatur.
passages.en: (That everyone be in a tithing. B) And we will that every free man over twelve years old (once he is twelve, G) who wishes to be entitled to clear himself [if accused] — or [if slain] to have his wergild paid — if anyone wishes to accuse him (strikes him down, B A), be brought into a hundred and into a tithing; otherwise let him (thereafter, G) not be entitled to any free man's rights.

passages.text: Siue paterfamilias siue cliens (sit, uolumus), ut omnis sit in centenario et fideiussione positus, et fideiussor eum seruet et ad omnem rectitudinem perducat.
passages.en: Whether he be a householder or a [household] follower: let each be brought into a hundred and under surety, and let the surety keep him and bring him to every legal obligation.

passages.text: Multus austerus homo uult (omne), si potest et sibi licet, tueri suum hominem utro modo, siue pro libero siue pro seruo, quo facilius eum tueri poterit; sed nolumus illam iniuriam pati.
passages.en: Many a powerful man wishes, if he can and may, to defend his man in court as whichever of the two seems to him easier to defend, either as a free man or as a slave; but we will not allow this injustice.

passages.text: Et uolumus, ut omnis homo duodennis iuret, quod numquam erit fur uel furis conscius (iuramento abrenunciet furto uel furti conscientie).
passages.en: (Of thieves. B) And (But, G) we will that every man over twelve years old swear this oath: that he will be neither a thief nor an accessory to a thief.

passages.text: Sitque omnis fidelis, qui calumpniosus non fuit, cuique nunquam defecit iuramentum uel Dei iudicium, in centenario simplici purgatione dignus.
passages.en: And let every trustworthy man who has not been of bad repute, and for whom neither oath nor ordeal has failed, be entitled to the single clearing [with oath-helpers of his own choosing] within the (his, A) hundred.

passages.text: Infideli autem eligantur iuramenta hominum in tribus centenariis, et triplex iuramentum tam late quam ad illam urbem pertinet; aut eat ad Dei iudicium.
passages.en: And for an untrustworthy man let [the court] choose the single oath [with helpers resident] in three hundreds [this and two neighbouring ones], and [if the judgment is for] the threefold oath, [helpers from the area] as far as belongs to that borough; or let him go to the ordeal.

passages.text: Simplexque purgatio attingatur simplici preiuramento et triplex triplici.
passages.en: And let [the plaintiff] compel the single clearing by a single fore-oath, and the threefold clearing by a threefold fore-oath.

passages.text: <ptr n="b" target="ConsCn_II-22-1b.lnote.oe.b-2"/>[<ptr n="b" target="ConsCn_II-22-1b.lnote.oe.b"/>Preiuramentum est unius hominis iurantis, antequam ille iuret qui Dei iudicium inire debet, et si contra illum qui ad<ptr n="1" target="ConsCn_II-22-1b.lnote.oe.1"/> Dei iudicium simplex uel ad Dei purgationem simplicem; triplex uero ad<ptr n="2" target="ConsCn_II-22-1b.lnote.oe.2"/> Dei iudicium uel purgatio attingi debet tribus preiurantibus.]
passages.en: [A fore-oath is that of one man swearing before he swears who must undergo the judgment of God; and if it is against one who goes to the simple judgment of God or to the simple purgation of God, it is simple [?]; but the threefold judgment of God or purgation must be reached with three swearing the fore-oath.]

notes.de: Der Satz (z. T. aus II 22, 1a; <hi rend="italic">vgl</hi>. 22, 2. 30, 3a) kann nach dem Wortschatz <hi rend="italic">præiuramentum</hi>, <hi rend="italic">attingere</hi> original sein, obwohl er sachlich 30, 3a widerspricht; <hi rend="italic">s. Gl</hi> Klageeid 13d. e; Ordal 33
notes.en: The sentence (partly from II 22, 1a; <hi rend="italic">cf</hi>. 22, 2. 30, 3a) may be original, to judge by the vocabulary <hi rend="italic">præiuramentum</hi>, <hi rend="italic">attingere</hi>, although in substance it contradicts 30, 3a; <hi rend="italic">see Gl</hi> Klageeid 13d. e; Ordal 33

notes.de: 22, 1<hi rend="italic">b aus Hk, verfasst <hi rend="spaced">vor</hi> Ordalabschaffung</hi> 1219, <hi rend="italic">jedoch, wenn vom Verf., nur nachträglich, da Hr fehlend. Vgl. S.</hi> 418<hi rend="superscript">b</hi>
notes.en: 22, 1b from Hk, composed <hi rend="italic">before</hi> the abolition of the ordeal in 1219, but, if by the author, only subsequently, since missing in Hr. Cf. p. 418<hi rend="superscript">b</hi>

passages.text: Et si procer (uel uirro) fidelem hominem habeat, quem ad preiuramentum pro se ponat, hoc illi licet; sin autem, ipsemet attingat.
passages.en: And if a thegn has a trustworthy man to swear the fore-oath for him, let it be so; if he has none, let him bring his suit himself.

passages.text: Nec unquam aliquod preiuramentum condonetur.
passages.en: And let no fore-oath ever be remitted.

passages.text: Neque quisquam ulla aduocacione tutacionis dignus sit, nisi habeat fidelem testem, unde hoc sibi contigit quod apud illum deprehenditur.
passages.en: And let no one [sued by attachment] be entitled to any vouching to warranty unless he has trustworthy witness as to where what is attached in his possession came to him from.

passages.text: Probetque idem testis in fidelitate Dei et domini sui, quod illi in uero testimonio sit, sicut ipse oculis uidit et auribus audiuit, quod ille recte illud nactus sit.
passages.en: And let the witness declare, by God's favour and his lord's, that it stands in true witness for him, as it saw with its eyes and heard with its ears, that he acquired it rightfully.

passages.text: Et nemo emat quicquam supra ualorem IIII denariorum, tam uiuum quam mortuum, nisi habeat fidele testimonium IIII hominum, siue urbi siue ruri.
passages.en: And let no one buy anything over four pennies' worth, either living or lying [dead chattels], unless he has the trustworthy witness of four men, whether it be in a borough or up in the country.

passages.text: Quodsi apud illum deprehensum fuerit, et huiusmodi testimonium non habuit, nulla sit aduocacio tutacionis, sed deprehensori suum reddat et prosolutam, et forisfacturam illi qui possidet.
passages.en: And if it is then attached, and he [the accused possessor] does not have such witness, let there be no vouching to warranty [allowed him], but let him give back to the owner his property together with a second payment of its value, and the fine to the one who owns it [the right to what the accused has forfeited].

passages.text: Si uero testimonium, sicut prediximus, habuit, ter fiat attestacio; tertio autem uendicet aut reddat illi cuius illud est.
passages.en: But if he [the accused possessor] has witness [of acquisition], as we have laid down here above (before, B?), then it [the attached item] may be vouched to warranty three times; the fourth time [the person vouched] must prove it his own or give it back to the one to whom it belongs.

passages.text: Neque enim nobis rectum uidetur, ut quisquam sibi uendicare deprehensum debeat, ubi fideles testes sint, et animaduerti possit, quod subductum sit, ut quisquam, inquam, deprehensum sibi uendicare debeat, ad citissimum ante sex menses, postquam subductum fuit.
passages.en: But it seems to us not right (no right, A) that anyone [sued by attachment] should be allowed to swear [the attached item] to be his own where there is witness [for the person robbed] and it can be recognised that there is fraud [on the possessor's part]: so that [henceforth] no one may claim it as his own until at the earliest six months after it was stolen.

passages.text: Et si quis calumpniatus fuerit et plebi suspectus et hos conuentus ter deuitauerit, quarto conuentu annominentur qui eum adeant et sub fideiussore ponant, si autem habere possit.
passages.en: And whoever is of bad repute and untrustworthy to the people, and avoids these courts three times: then let [men] be chosen (appointed, A) from the fourth court to ride to him; and let him find a surety even then, if he can.

passages.text: Quodsi fideiussores inuenire nequiuerint, uincant illum utrum poterunt, siue uiuum siue mortuum, et accipiant quicquid habet.
passages.en: But if he cannot [do this], (then, A) let him be overpowered however one can, alive or dead; and let them take everything he has (had, G).

passages.text: Et reddant callumpniatori suum censum capitalem; residui uero dimidium domini sit ipsius, et dimidium centenarii.
passages.en: And let the plaintiff be paid [from it] his compensation, and of the rest let the lord [of the criminal] take half, (and, B) the hundred half.

passages.text: Quodsi uter siue cognatus siue alienus illum aditum recusauerit, soluat regi CXX solidos.
passages.en: And if either a kinsman [of the criminal] or a stranger (man, B) refuses this riding, let him pay the king 120 shillings.

passages.text: Manifestus autem fur uel qui in domini prodicione extiterit, quicquid adeat usquam, nunquam salutem adquirat.
passages.en: (Of thieves. B) And let the manifest thief, or whoever is found guilty of treachery against his lord, seek [sanctuary] wherever he may: they are never to obtain [security of] life.

passages.text: Et qui se uel suum hominem in placito defenderit contracalumpniis, totum illud sit perlocutum, et tamen calumpnianti satisfaciat iuxta decretum centenarii.
passages.en: And whoever in court defends himself or his man by counter-accusation(s?), let all of it count as said in vain, and let him answer his opponent as seems right to the hundred.

passages.text: Nec quisquam suscipiat quemquam diucius quam tribus noctibus, nisi ipse illum commendet, cui olim seruierat.
passages.en: And that no one receive any man for longer than three nights unless the one whom he previously served commends him.

passages.text: Neque quisquam suum seruientem licenciet, donec mundus sit ab omni precedente querimonia.
passages.en: And let no one dismiss his man from him before he is clear of every charge on which he was previously accused.

passages.text: Et si quis furi obuius factus fuerit et illum sponte abire permiserit sine exclamatione, emendet secundum furis redempcionem uel se ipsum pleno iuramento purget, quod ipse cum illo nullum scelus esse sciebat.
passages.en: And if anyone meets a thief and deliberately lets him go without raising the hue and cry, let him pay compensation at the thief's wergild or clear himself with a full oath that he knew of no crime in him.

passages.text: Et qui exclamacionem audierit et accurrere neglexerit, soluat despectum regis uel plena lege se purget.
passages.en: And if anyone hears the hue and cry and neglects [to follow] it, let him pay [the fine for] disobedience to the king or clear himself fully.

passages.text: Et si quis centenario adeo suspectus est adeoque calumpniosus, ut a tribus calumpniatoribus simul calumpnietur, tunc nichil aliud fiat, nisi quod ad triplex Dei iudicium eat.
passages.en: (The very untrustworthy. B) And if anyone is so untrustworthy to the hundred and so often accused, and three men then accuse him together, then let there be nothing else [left for him] but to go to the threefold ordeal.

passages.text: Quodsi dominus illius asserat, quod ille numquam in iuramento uel de iudicio cecidisset, postquam conuentus factus est apud Wincestriam, assumat ipse dominus sibi duos fideles de ipso centenario, qui secum iurent, quod illi numquam defecerat iuramentum uel Dei iudicium, nec unquam furis tributum soluerat, nisi prepositum habeat qui hoc facere pro illo dignus sit.
passages.en: But if his lord asserts that neither oath nor ordeal has failed him since the assembly at Winchester, let the lord take two trustworthy men within that [one] hundred, and [these three] are to swear ‘that neither oath nor ordeal ever failed him, nor did he have to pay theft-compensation’ — unless [the lord] has a reeve who is entitled to do this [in place of the lord].

passages.text: Si ergo illud iuramentum perfectum fuerit, eligat tunc calumpniatus utrum maluerit, siue simplex Dei iudicium siue libram ualens iuramentum de tribus centenariis, supra triginta denarios.
passages.en: If this oath then succeeds, let the man who is accused choose whichever of the two [means of clearing himself] he wishes: either the single ordeal or an oath worth 1 pound [of silver], [with helpers] from no further away than three hundreds [this one and two neighbouring ones]: [for an object] over 30 pence.

passages.text: Quodsi ipsi illud iuramentum facere non audeant, calumpniatus triplex Dei iudicium adeat.
passages.en: (Of the ordeal. B) But if they [the lord and helpers] do not dare to give the oath, let [the accused] go to the threefold ordeal.

passages.text: Quod calumpniator sic attingat: assumat V et ipse sit sextus.
passages.en: And let [the plaintiff] compel (obtain, Inst. H) the threefold ordeal as follows: let him take five [oath-helpers] and be himself the sixth in the [accusing] oath.

passages.text: Si autem calumpniatus in ipso iudicio deciderit, prima uice emendet calumpniatori duplum et suo domino suam redempcionem, qui forisfactura illius dignus sit, deinde ponat fideiussores, quod deinceps tale facinus cauebit.
passages.en: And if [the accused] is then found guilty, let him pay the plaintiff double [the damage] the first time, and the lord — [if] he is entitled (to it, A) to the fine [to be forfeited by the accused] — his wergild, and provide trustworthy sureties [to the effect] that he will refrain from all wrongdoing in future.

passages.text: Quodsi iterum tale facere presumpserit et Dei iudicio conuictus fuerit, nullam redempcionem habeat, quin ei truncentur manus aut pedes aut utrumque, iuxta quod peccati quantitas exegerit.
passages.en: And if he is found guilty the second time, let there be no other compensation than that his hands or his feet or both be cut off, according to what the deed is.

passages.text: Quodsi maius expetit, oculi eius eruantur, et nasus curtetur, auresque cum superiore labro abscindantur, aut pilletur, quod horum illi decreuerunt [qui] consulere debent, quomodo possint et peccationem corrigere et anime illius parcere.
passages.en: And if he has then committed still greater wrong, let his eyes be put out, and let them cut off his nose and his ears and his upper lip, or scalp him, whichever of these [punishments] is then decided on (or wished, B) — [namely] by those who are to decide on it —: thus one can (must, B) punish and yet also spare the soul.

passages.text: Qui si sub fideiussione effugerit et Dei iudicium sic deuitauerit, soluat fideiussor calumpniatori capitalem censum et regi redempcionem eius uel illi qui forisfactura illius dignus sit.
passages.en: But if [the accused] escapes and avoids the ordeal, let the surety pay the plaintiff his compensation for the goods, and [the accused's] wergild to the king or to the one who is entitled to the fine (wergild, B) [forfeited by the accused].

passages.text: Quodsi ipse dominus calumpniis subiaceat, quod eius consilio malefactor et primum illud facinus perpetrauit et tandem effugit, assumat sibi V fideles et ipse sextus sit et ab hiis se (iuramento) purget.
passages.en: And if the lord is accused of the man having escaped on his advice and of having done wrong before, let him take five trustworthy (men, B) [as oath-helpers] and be himself the sixth, and clear himself of it.

passages.text: Que purgacio si perfecta fuerit, sit dominus dignus illa redempcione accipienda.
passages.en: If the clearing succeeds, let him be entitled to that wergild [of his dependant].

passages.text: Si autem defecerit (purgatio), redempcio (furis) contingat regi; fur autem sit exlex erga uniuersum populum.
passages.en: And if it does not succeed, let the king take that wergild. And let the thief be an outlaw with respect to the whole people.

passages.text: Omnis etiam dominus habeat suos domesticos in sua propria fideiussione.
passages.en: (Of household men. B) And let every lord keep his household men under his own surety.

passages.text: Et si quis illum accusauerit, secundum legem respondeat in illo centenario, in quo accusatus sit.
passages.en: And if [the household man] is accused of anything, let him answer within the hundred in which he is accused, as is the proper law.

passages.text: Quodsi accusatus effugiat, soluat dominus illius regi redempcionem eius.
passages.en: And if he is accused but escapes, let the lord pay the king the wergild of that man.

passages.text: Si uero ipse dominus accusatus fuerit, illum suo consilio effugisse, purget se cum quinque suis paribus et ipse sit sextus.
passages.en: And if the lord is accused of the man having escaped on his advice, let him clear himself with five thegns and be himself the sixth [in the oath].

passages.text: Cui si purgacio deficiat, soluat eius redempcionem regi; ille uero sit exlex.
passages.en: If this clearing fails him, let him pay the king his wergild. And let that man be an outlaw (with respect to the king, B).

passages.text: Seruus qui Dei iudicio nocens apparuerit, prima uice signetur.
passages.en: And if a slave (thief, B A?) is found guilty at the ordeal, let him (then, B) be branded the first time.

passages.text: Secunda autem uice nulla redempcio sit nisi caput.
passages.en: And the second time let there be no other compensation there than the head.

passages.text: Et si quis toti populo suspectus sit, prepositus regis eum adeat et sub fideiussione ponat, ut, si quis eum calumpniatus fuerit, satisfaciat.
passages.en: (Of untrustworthy men. B) And if there is anyone who is untrustworthy to all the people, let the king's reeve intervene and bring (let them bring, G A) him under surety, so that he may be brought to justice for those who accuse him.

passages.text: Qui si fideiussorem habere nequeat, . . . et inmundo sepelliatur.
passages.en: But if he gets no (such, G?) surety, let him be killed and laid in a dishonoured [grave].

passages.text: Quodsi quisquam obstiterit, uterque eidem iuri subiaceat.
passages.en: And if anyone defends him [by force], let them both be subject to the same legal penalty.

passages.text: Et si quis hoc neglexerit et secundum omnium [nost]rum institutum perficere noluerit, det regi CXX solidos.
passages.en: And whoever neglects this and will not further it, as is the decision of us all, let him pay the king 120 shillings.

passages.text: Inter urbes quoque sit una lex in purgacione.
passages.en: And let there be one law of clearing among the boroughs.

passages.text: Et si quis alienigena uel suffragio amicorum destitutus adeo anxiatus sit amicorum penuria, quod fideiussorem habere nequeat, in prima accusacione, subeat suspendium et ibi prestoletur, donec adeat Dei iudicium et ibi proficiat quod poterit.
passages.en: (Of men without kin. B) And if a man without kin or one come from afar is so hard pressed through lack of kin that he has no surety, then, at the first accusation, let him submit to imprisonment and wait there until he goes to God's ordeal, and fare there as he may.

passages.text: Certe quicunque alienigene uel amicis carenti peius iudicium quam suo socio (sodali) iudicauerit, sibimet ipsi nocet.
passages.en: Truly, whoever gives a worse judgment to a man without kin and one come from afar than to his own fellow harms himself.

passages.text: Eṭ si quis mendacium super sacrato iurauerit et conuictus fuerit, amittat manum aut dimidiam redempcionem sui, quę communis sit domino et episcopo.
passages.en: (Of false oaths. B) And if anyone swears a false oath on relics and is convicted, let him lose the [swearing] hand or half [his] wergild; and let the latter be shared between the lord [of the court] and the bishop.

passages.text: Nec sit deinceps iuramento dignus, nisi erga Deum plene satisfecerit et fideiussorem dederit, se deinceps ab huiusmodi obseruaturum.
passages.en: And let him not be oath-worthy thereafter, unless he atones all the more deeply before God and finds a surety that he will always refrain from such [perjury] afterwards.

passages.text: Et si quis falsum testimonium manifeste tulerit et de hoc conuictus fuerit, testimonium illius imperpetuum fide careat, sed soluat regi aut domino regionis per collicipium.
passages.en: (Of false witness. B) And if anyone openly stands in false witness and is [then] convicted, let his witness count for nothing thereafter, but let him pay the king or the landlord (who has jurisdiction over him, G) [an amount equal to] his healsfang.

passages.text: Nullo quidem tempore iniuria permissa est fieri; sed tamen festis diebus et sacratis locis debet quisque diligentissime parcere.
passages.en: Wrong is permitted at no time; but one must guard against it most carefully at festivals (and fasts, G) and in holy places.

passages.text: Et quanto quis potentior est uel maioris ordinis, tanto debet ille altius secundum Deum et seculum iniuriam patratam corrigere.
passages.en: And the more powerful or the higher in rank anyone is, the more deeply must he atone for wrong before God and before the world.

passages.text: Diuinaque correctio ex librorum decretis et secularis ex seculari lege inquiratur.
passages.en: And let spiritual atonement always be sought eagerly according to the teaching (the word, B A) of the [canonical] books, and let secular compensation be sought according to secular law.

passages.text: Si quis ministrum altaris peremerit, sit ille exlex et erga Deum et erga homines, nisi ipse non solum uago exilio plene delictum correxerit, set et cognacioni satisfecerit; aut purgamine uirili se purget.
passages.en: (If anyone kills a priest. B) If anyone kills a servant of the altar, let him be an outlaw before God and men, unless he atones all the more deeply by a pilgrimage of exile, and also [makes amends] to the kindred [of the slain] — or let him clear himself by an oath [to the amount of the victim's] wergild —;

passages.text: Satisfactionem autem suscipiat infra XXX dies tam erga Deum quam erga homines supra omnia que sunt.
passages.en: and within thirty nights let him begin to make amends both to God and to men, on [pain of losing] all that he has.

passages.text: Si quis ordinatum aut alienigenam utro leserit substantia aut uita, tunc debet rex ei esse pro cognato et propinquo, nisi ille alium habeat.
passages.en: If anyone in any way wrongs a man in holy orders or a foreigner, in property or in life, then the king shall be to him in place of a kinsman and protector — unless he has another (lord, G) —,

passages.text: Regique satisfaciat, aut ipse delictum acriter uindicet:
passages.en: and let compensation be paid to the king as is fitting, or let him avenge the deed very severely.

passages.text: Christianum regem oportet iustissime Dei offensionem ulcisci acerrime iuxta delicti qualitatem.
passages.en: It very rightly befits a Christian king to avenge offences against God very severely, according to what the deed is.

passages.text: Si minister altaris homicidium aut aliud criminale peccatum pat[ra]uerit, careat tam ordinibus quam dignitate delictumque corrigat uago exilio, sicut ei papa decreuerit.
passages.en: (Of men in orders. B) If a servant of the altar becomes a slayer or otherwise commits too grievous a misdeed, then let him lose both his orders and his homeland [with his civil rank], and go into exile on pilgrimage as far as the Pope prescribes for him, and do eager penance.

passages.text: Quodsi in[fi]cias geret, triplici purgamine se purget.
passages.en: But if he wishes to clear himself, let him clear himself with the threefold [proof].

passages.text: Et nisi infra XXX dies satisfactionem inceperit, sit exlex tam erga Deum quam aput homines.
passages.en: And unless he begins to make amends to God and men within thirty nights, let him be an outlaw.

passages.text: Si quis ordinatum liget aut [uerber]et aut nimiis contumeliis afficiat, primum satisfaciat ei secundum quod rectum est, deinde episcopo emendam altaris soluat iuxta ordinis dignitatem dominoque aut regi per plenam montam; aut pleno purgamine se purget.
passages.en: (That no one bind or beat a man in orders. B) If anyone binds or beats or grossly insults a man in orders, let him make amends to him as is right, and to the bishop with altar-compensation according to the rank of [the injured man's] orders, and to the [immunity-]lord or the king with full compensation for breach of protection; or let him clear himself with a full clearing.

passages.text: [43] Si ordinatus se forisfaciat crimine mortali, superetur et ad episcopi iudicium custodiatur iuxta facti qualitatem.
passages.en: If a man in orders forfeits himself by a capital offence, let him be seized and held for the bishop's judgment, according to what the deed is.

passages.text: [44] Si morte dampnatus confessionis colloquium petat, nemo prohibeat.
passages.en: If a man condemned to death asks for confession, let it never be refused him.

passages.text: [44, 1] Qui autem prohibuerit, soluat regi CXX solidos; si uero inficiari uoluerit, sic se purget: producat V et ipse sit sextus.
passages.en: And if anyone refuses [it] him, let him pay the king 120 shillings in compensation for it; or let him clear himself: let him take five [oath-helpers] and be himself the sixth [in the oath].

passages.text: [45] Si autem fieri potest, nunquam die Dominica quisquam morte dampnatus morti detur (decrete), nisi fugiens aut repugnans sit; sed pocius superetur et seruetur, donec dies festi preterita sit.
passages.en: If it can be managed, let no condemned man ever be put to death during the Sunday festival — unless he flees or fights [against arrest] —, but let him be overpowered and held [until] the feast-day has passed.

passages.text: [45, 1] Si liber die festa operetur, emendet hoc collicipio; presertim erga Deum diligenter hoc emendet, sicut sibi iniunctum fuerit.
passages.en: (Of keeping feast-days. B) If a free man works on a feast-day, then let him pay compensation for it with his healsfang; and above all let him atone for it eagerly before God, as he is instructed.

passages.text: [45, 2] Si uero seruus, amittat cutem aut cutis redempcionem iuxta operis qualitatem.
passages.en: A slave, if he works, let him lose his hide [be flogged] or pay hide-money, according to what the deed is.

passages.text: [45, 3] Si autem dominus seruum suum festo in[ui]tum operari compellat, amittat illum seruum; sitque liber populariter seruus ille; et dominus soluat legis transgressionem aput Danos, forisfacturam apud Anglos iuxta qualitatem facti; aut se purget.
passages.en: If a lord compels his slave to work on a feast-day, let him lose the slave; and let the latter thereafter be free [in folk-law]; and let the lord pay lahslit among the Danes, a fine among the English, according to what the deed is; or let him clear himself.

passages.text: [46] Si liber legitimum ieiunium infregerit, soluat legis transgressionem aput Danos, forisfacturam apud Anglos iuxta qualitatem facti.
passages.en: (Of fasting. B) If a free man breaks a lawful fast, let him pay lahslit among the Danes, a fine among the English, according to what the deed is.

passages.text: [46, 1] Malum quidem est, ut quis die ieiunii ante horam commedit, peius uero, se ut escis carnium inquinet.
passages.en: It is bad that anyone should eat before mealtime in a lawful fast, and still worse (is it, B) that anyone should defile himself with meat.

passages.text: [46, 2] Quod si seruus faciat, amittat cutem aut cutis redempcionem iuxta facti qualitatem.
passages.en: If a slave does it, let him lose his hide [be flogged] or [pay] hide-money, according to what the deed is.

passages.text: [47] Si quis manifeste quadragesimalem obseruacionem transgreditur siue sedicione siue nupciis siue rapina siue quoquam magnifico peccato, dupliciter hoc corrigatur secundum peccati modum, sic et in reuerenda solempnitate.
passages.en: If anyone openly breaks the Lenten fast by fighting or by intercourse or by robbery or by any grave misdeed, let it be subject to double compensation, as (also, B) on a high feast-day, according to what the deed is.

passages.text: [48] Si quis diuinam rectitudinem armis prohibet, soluat legis transgressionem aput Danos, plenam forisfacturam aput Anglos, aut se purget sic: producat XI et ipse sit duodecimus.
passages.en: (If anyone withholds God's dues. B) If anyone withholds God's dues by force, let him pay lahslit among the Danes, the full fine among the English, or clear himself: let him take eleven (men, B) [as helpers] and be himself the twelfth [in the oath].

passages.text: [48, 1] Qui si ibi hominem uulneret, emendet illud, et soluat plenam forisfacturam domino, et [ab] episcopo manus redimat aut illas amittat.
passages.en: If he wounds someone, let him make amends for it [to the injured man] and pay the full fine to the [immunity-]lord, and redeem his hands from the bishop or lose them.

passages.text: [48, 2] Si autem hominem occidat, sit exlex, et eum prosequa[tu]r [cum] -dampno quicumque amator iusticie est.
passages.en: If he kills a man [in doing so], let him be an outlaw, and let everyone who desires right pursue him with the hue and cry.

passages.text: [48, 3] Si uero efficit, ut quis eum ibi occidat, uiribus uolendo iusticie resistere, si hoc probari potest, iaceat insolubilis.
passages.en: If he brings it about that he is killed because he fights against right, if that is proved (can be proved, B), let him lie uncompensated [to his kin by the slayer].

passages.text: [49] Si quis ordinis fracturam facit, emendet hoc iuxta ordinis dignitatem: siue per redempcionem siue per forisfacturam siue per legis transgressionem siue per totam substantiam suam.
passages.en: If anyone commits a violation of holy orders, let him make amends according to the rank of [the injured man's] orders: either by [his] wergild or by a fine or by lahslit or by [his] whole property.

passages.text: [50] Si quis legale institutum transgreditur, emendet hoc iuxta modum facti:
passages.en: (Of adultery. B) If anyone commits adultery, let him make amends for it according to what the deed is:

passages.text: [50, 1] Mala quidem legalis instituti transgressio est, ut quis cum uacua concumbat, peior uero cum desponsata uel cum sacrata.
passages.en: It is a bad adultery when a married man fornicates with an unmarried woman, and much worse with another man's wife or with a woman consecrated [to God].

passages.text: [51] Si quis cum cognata concumbit, emendet illud iuxta modum cognacionis, siue per redempcionem siue per forisfacturam siue per totam substanciam:
passages.en: (Of incest. B) If anyone commits incest, let him make amends according to the degree of kinship: either by [his] wergild or by a fine or by [his] whole property.

passages.text: [51, 1] Non sunt equipollencia cum sorore concumbere et cum ea que remocior sit cognacione.
passages.en: It is not the same whether one lies with a sister or whether it were a distant relative.

passages.text: [52] Si quis cum uidua inuita concumbit, corrigat hoc per redempcionem.
passages.en: (Of widows. B) If anyone takes a widow by force, let him make amends for it with (his, B) wergild.

passages.text: [53] Si coniugata, uiuente uiro suo, cum alio concubuerit, et hoc manifestum fuerit, fiat inperpetuum dedecus deinceps sibimet; et omnia que illius fuerant habeat uir; ipsa uero amittat nasum et aures.
passages.en: (That no wife should whore. B) If, in her husband's lifetime, a wife whores with another man, and this becomes undeniable, let her then become a shame before men to herself, and let the husband receive all that she possessed (possesses, B); and let her lose (then both, B) nose and (as well as, B) ears.

passages.text: [53, 1] Quodsi inficiata fuerit et purgamine defecerit, cadat in manus episcopi, qui inde acriter iudicet.
passages.en: If, however, it is [only] a [deniable] accusation, and the clearing [oath] fails, then let the bishop dispose and judge strictly.

passages.text: [54] Si coniugatus cum propria ancilla concumbit, amittat illam et satisfaciat pro se ipso tam erga Deum quam erga homines.
passages.en: If a married man whores with his own slave-woman, let him lose her and atone for himself before God and before men.

passages.text: [54, 1] Qui [tamen] simul habuit uxorem et concubinam, nemo presbiter faciat ei rectitudinem quamquam, que Christiano fieri debeat, donec cessauerit et delictum correxerit, sicut ei episcopus iniunxerit.
passages.en: And whoever has a wife and besides her a concubine, let no priest perform for him any of those [soul's-health] services which one owes to perform for a Christian man, before he desists [from concubinage] and atones as deeply as the bishop prescribes to him, and is willing in future to desist from such.

passages.text: [55] Alienigene qui suam uenerem corrigere neggligunt, a patria cum sua substantia et peccato discedant.
passages.en: Foreign men, if they will not make their sexual relations lawful, shall depart (let them be driven, B) from the land with their goods and (in, B) sins.

passages.text: [56] Si mortificat[ur]a manifesta fuerit, malefactor cognatis tradatur.
passages.en: If an undeniable secret murder happens, so that a person is destroyed (murdered, A), let [the killer] (the murderer, B) be handed over to the kinsmen [of the slain].

passages.text: [56, 1] Quodsi accusacio sit, et inficianti purgamine male succedat, episcopi iudicium subeat.
passages.en: If, however, it is a [deniable] accusation and the clearing [oath] fails, let the bishop judge.

passages.text: [57] Si quis aduersus regem uel dominum arma tulerit, sit reus et uite et uniuerse substancie, nisi triplici Dei iudicio se absoluere potuerit.
passages.en: (Treason against a lord. B) If anyone treacherously plots against the king or the (his, B) lord, let him be liable [to the loss] of his life and of everything he possesses, unless he goes to the threefold ordeal (and is found clean there, B).

passages.text: [58] Si quis regis fideiussionem soluerit, emendet hoc V libris;
passages.en: (Of the breach of protection. B) If anyone violates the king's protection, let him atone for it with 5 pounds [to the king].

passages.text: [58, 1] qui autem archiepiscopi uel basilide, III libris;
passages.en: If anyone violates the protection of an archbishop or of a royal prince, let him atone for it [to him] with 3 pounds.

passages.text: [58, 2] qui uero plebei episcopi aut principis, duas libras soluat.
passages.en: If anyone violates the protection (stronghold, A) of a diocesan bishop or of an ealdorman, let him atone for it [to him] with 2 pounds.

passages.text: [59] Si quis in curia regis sedicionem mouerit, amittat uitam, nisi quid ei rex misericordie prestare uoluerit (dignatus fuerit).
passages.en: (Of him who fights at the king's court. B) If anyone fights at the king's court, let him lose his life, unless the king will grant him mercy.

passages.text: [60] Si quis iniuste quemquam dearmauerit, soluat illi collicipium; si autem ligauerit, soluat illi dimidium redempcionis eius (id est: IIII l.).
passages.en: (Of disarming another man. B) If anyone wrongfully disarms a man, let him pay for him with his healsfang; and if anyone binds him, let him pay with half [his] wergild.

passages.text: [61] Si quis in exercitu pacem plene fregerit, amittat uitam uel uite (dignitatem, scilicet) redempcionem.
passages.en: (Breach of special peace. B) If anyone commits a full[-weight] breach of special peace [by homicide] in the army, let him lose life or [his] wergild.

passages.text: [61, 1] Si uero semifecerit, emendet iuxta modum facti.
passages.en: If he commits a half[-weight breach of peace], let him atone (for it, G) according to what the deed is.

passages.text: [62] Si quis domi inuasionem fecerit, emendet hoc V libris erga regem in lege Anglorum, in lege autem Danorum sicut prius institutum fuit.
passages.en: (Housebreaking. B) If anyone commits [unlawful] attack on a house, let him atone for it with 5 pounds to the king under English law (and in Kent, from the house-attack [penalty], 5 [pounds belong] to the king and 3 to the archbishop, G), and under Danish law as it has stood hitherto.

passages.text: [62, 1] Si autem ibi peremptus fuerit, iaceat insolubilis.
passages.en: And if he is slain in doing so, let him lie dead without being paid for [to his kin].

passages.text: Si quis rapinam patrauerit, soluat et persoluat, et sit reus sue redempcionis erga regem.
passages.en: (Robbery. B) If anyone commits robbery, let him return [it] and pay [it] again, and be liable for his wergild to the king (or to the one who holds jurisdiction over him, G).

passages.text: Domi fractura, combustura, manifestum furtum, patens mortificatura (scilicet clancula occisio que non possit negari) dominique prodicio secundum legem seculi carent emendatione.
passages.en: (Housebreaking. B) Housebreaking and arson and openly proven theft and undeniable secret murder and treachery against one's lord are, under secular law, not to be atoned for [with money].

passages.text: Si quis urbis refectionem siue pontis refectionem siue exercitus it[in]eracionem neglexerit, soluat regi CXX solidos in lege Anglorum, et in lege Danorum sicut prius institutum fuit; aut se purget sic: annominentur illi XIIII, et perquirat X[I].
passages.en: (Repair of fortifications. B) If anyone neglects the repair of fortifications or the making-ready of bridges or service in the army, let him atone to the king under English law with 120 shillings, and under Danish law as it has held hitherto; or let him clear himself by oath: let [the court] name 14 for him, and let him win 11 [of them as his oath-helpers].

passages.text: Si quis autem Dei commodum tenet contra ius, reddat et persoluat ei cui oportet; regi autem persoluat suam redempcionem.
passages.en: (Concerning one outlawed by the church court. B) If anyone unlawfully keeps with him a fugitive from [the legal claim of] the Church [an outlaw], let him hand him over to the court (lawfully, B) and pay the [lord of the court] to whom it is due [to receive the fine for harbouring the recalcitrant]; and let him pay (him, A, wrongly) to the king with (his, G) wergild.

passages.text: Si quis excommunicatum tenet et seruat, caueat sibimet et uniuerse substantie sue.
passages.en: If anyone keeps with him and maintains an excommunicated person or an outlaw, let him bring danger [of forfeiture] upon his life and his whole standing in property.

passages.text: Si quis autem ab iniusticia sua ad iusticiam conuerti uoluerit, misericordia super eum fiat propter timorem Domini, in quantum misericordie racio expostulauerit.
passages.en: And if anyone is willing to turn back from wrong to the order of law, let one take pity, out of fear of God, as best one can, very willingly on him.

passages.text: Faciamus etiam, ut nobis est ualde necessarium: semper succurramus ei cicius, qui succursu magis indiget; et accipiemus inde premium, ubi acceptabilius est.
passages.en: And let us act as is our duty: always help first the one who most needs help; then we shall carry off (gather in, A, Quadr.) the reward for it there where it is most valuable to us.

passages.text: Debemus etiam inbecillem propter amorem et timorem Dei micius iudicare quam fortem et discernere,
passages.en: (Of the weak. B) For one must always, out of love and fear of God, award judgment and spiritual penance more mildly to the weak man than to the strong;

passages.text: cum nequeat (quemadmodum indubitanter scimus) inualid[u]s et ualido, infirm[u]s et sano eque onus sustinere.
passages.en: because the powerless man, [as] we know (can know, B) right well, cannot lift (bear, B) an equal (great, B) burden [with] the strong, nor the sick man [one] equal to the healthy.

passages.text: Debemus itaque moderari, discrete distinguere senium et iuuentam, opes et inopiam, libertatem et seruitutem, egritudinem et sanitatem.
passages.en: And therefore we must moderate and sensibly distinguish age and youth, wealth (the rich, B) and poverty, freedom and slavery (free men and slaves, B), health and sickness (the healthy and the sick, B).

passages.text: Non solum in diuinis decretis sed etiam in secularibus iudiciis hec sunt distinguenda.
passages.en: And one must distinguish these circumstances both in spiritual penances and in secular judgments (judgment, B).

passages.text: Eciam in multis factis, cum quis ex necessitate peccat, tanto iustius ei impe[n]denda est misericordia, quanto magis eum necessitas ad malefactum impulit.
passages.en: Further, in many a (joint, B) misdeed, when someone [has been] a doer under compulsion, then this (man, B) is the more worthy of protection, the more he has done what he did out of compulsion.

passages.text: Et si quis quicquam imprudenter fecerit, non erit consimile, ac si prudenter factum fuisset.
passages.en: And if anyone does something unintentionally, that is not wholly the same as (as the one, B) who does it intentionally (as its happening intentionally, G).

passages.text: De libertatibus post concessis. Hoc est autem alleuamen, quod uniuerse genti mee parcere uolo, a quibus ante hec nimium erant g[rau]ati.
passages.en: The following, now, is the relief by which I wish to give all the people protection [against that] with which they have hitherto been all too greatly oppressed.

passages.text: Primum quidem, quod edico omnibus meis prepositis, ut in meo proprio recte laborent et me inde procurent, et deinde, quod eis nemo debet quicquam largiri in adiutorio mee procuracionis, nisi spontanea benignitate aliquid eis impendere uelit.
passages.en: Namely, first of all, that I command all my reeves that they manage my own estate (for me, G) properly and provision me from it, and that no one need give them anything as a contribution to provisioning, unless he himself wishes.

passages.text: Quodsi quis ab eo forisfacturam exegerit, redempcionis sue reus sit erga regem.
passages.en: And if after this [time] anyone [of the reeves] demands a fine [for hospitality], let him be liable for his wergild to the king.

passages.text: Et si quis forte sine detestacione ex hac uita migrauerit, siue propter in[c]uriam siue propter mortem subitaneam, dominus illius non uendicet sibi quicquam amplius de ipsius possessione nisi sua iusta excercitualia.
passages.en: (Concerning heriot. B) And if anyone (someone, B) departs this life without a last disposition [for church and lord], whether [it was left undone] through his negligence or through sudden death, then let the lord take from his movable goods no(thing, B) more than his proper heriot [war-gear].

passages.text: Sed possessio intestati ipsius ex dispositione illius rectissime diuidatur uxori prolique et cognatis, cuique iuxta modum oportunum.
passages.en: Rather, let the property be distributed, under his direction, most justly to wife and children and near kinsmen, to each according to the measure that is due to him.

passages.text: Exercitualia uero ita s[i]nt moderata, ut tollerabile sit.
passages.en: And let the heriots be fixed in such a way as befits [each one's] rank:

passages.text: Comitis, sicut decet, que sunt VIII equi, quatuor sellati et IIII non sellati, IIII galee et IIII lorice, octo lancee et totidem scuta, IIII gladii necnon ducente mance auri.
passages.en: (Of an earl. B) An earl's, as belongs to it, namely 8 horses, 4 saddled and 4 unsaddled, and 4 helmets and 4 mail-coats and 8 spears and as many shields and 4 swords and 200 mancuses [25 pounds] of gold.

passages.text: Uironis uero regis, qui est proximus ei: quatuor equi, duo cum sellis et duo sine sellis, duo gladii, quatuor lancee et totidem scuta, galea una et lorica I necnon et L mance auri.
passages.en: (Of a king's thegn. B) And then (the heriot of, B) the king's thegns who stand closest to him [the king]: 4 horses, 2 saddled and 2 unsaddled, and 2 swords and 4 spears and as many shields and [1] helmet and mail-coat and 50 mancuses [6¼ pounds] of gold.

passages.text: Minoris uero uirronis: equus et apparatus eius (id est sella, frenum) et armatura eius aut collicipium illius aput Westsexam; et aput Mircen. due libre et apud Orientales Anglos due libre.
passages.en: (Of another thegn. B) And of lesser thegns: [1] horse and its harness and his weapons, or [instead of all that] his healsfang [120 shillings] in Wessex; and in Mercia 2 pounds [120 Mercian shillings] and in East Anglia 2 pounds.

passages.text: Et uirronis excercitualia apud Danos, qui suum priuilegium habeat: quatuor libre.
passages.en: And in the land among the Danes, the heriot of a king's thegn who has his own jurisdiction: 4 pounds [of silver].

passages.text: Quodsi apud regem maiorem familiaritatem habeat: duo equi, unus cum sella et alter sine sella, unus gladius et due lancee et duo scuta et L mance auri.
passages.en: And if he has a closer relationship to the king: 2 horses, 1 saddled and the other unsaddled, and 1 sword and 2 spears and 2 shields and 50 mancuses of gold.

passages.text: Eius uero qui impotencior apud regem: due libre.
passages.en: And he who (has less and, B) is less well-off: 2 pounds [of silver].

passages.text: Uir autem quod uiuens tenuit sine calumpnia, post decessum uiri teneat uxor illius idem et filii sine calumpnia.
passages.en: And where the free householder has sat unchallenged and unaccused (all his life, B), on that same [homestead] let the wife and the children sit undisputed.

passages.text: Quodsi uir ante obitum (suum) calumpniatus fuerit, illo mortuo, respondeant heredes sui calumpniis, ut ipse deberet.
passages.en: If, however, that householder was accused before he was dead, then the heirs must answer, as he himself would have to if he had life.

passages.text: Uidua uero per spacium unius anni se contineat in uiduitate sua; post eligat quod sibi placeat.
passages.en: (Of the widow, that she should remain twelve months without a husband. B) And let every widow remain without a husband for twelve months; (and, B) afterwards let her choose what she herself wishes.

passages.text: Quodsi infra annum uirum eligat, amittat dotem et omnia, que possidet per priorem uirum, tam in terra quam in mobili substantia; que cadant in iura agnatorum proximorum prioris mariti.
passages.en: But if she (then, B) chooses a husband within the space of a (the, B) year, then let her lose that morning-gift and all those goods which she received through the former husband; and let the nearest kinsmen [of the latter] take possession of the land (the landed estates, G) and the property which she has held until now.

passages.text: Ipse autem posterior uir sit reus redempcionis sue erga regem aut erga illum, cui rex concessit, scilicet dominum, qui priuilegium habet in forefacturis suorum.
passages.en: And let the [second husband] be liable for his wergild to the king or to the one to whom the king has granted it (jurisdiction over him, G).

passages.text: Que etiam si ui rapta sit, careat per alium possessis, nisi illum relinqueret, numquam illius futura.
passages.en: And even if she is taken as wife by force, let her lose the goods [of the first marriage], unless she wishes to go back home again from the [second] man and never afterwards becomes his.

passages.text: Nec uidua aliqua nimium cito sacretur.
passages.en: And let a widow never be consecrated [to God] too hastily.

passages.text: Omnis autem uidua exercitualia debita infra anni spacium sine forisfacto persoluat, nisi ei cicius facultas persoluendi sit.
passages.en: And let every widow pay the heriot within twelve months [after her husband's death] without penalty [for delay], unless it suits her earlier.

passages.text: Nec quisquam cogat mulierem uiduam uel uirginem ad hoc quod sibi displiceat, neque pro censu uendat, nisi qu[i]d ipse sua sponte dare uelit.
passages.en: And let neither a [widowed] woman nor a maiden (ever, B) be forced (taken, A) to [a man] who displeases her herself, nor sold for money, unless the [suitor] is willing of his own accord to give something [to her guardian].

passages.text: [75] Iustum eciam censeo, quod, si quis, alienam domum ingressurus causa rei cuiuspiam agende, ibi lanceam suam extra ostium statuat uel aliam armaturam pacifice locet, ubi quiete posset esse, si liceret, et alius illud armature arripiat et dampnum quodpiam ex ea perpetret,
passages.en: (Of someone setting his spear at another's door. B) And I deem it right (will, A): if anyone sets his (own, B) spear at the house-door of another man, having business inside there, or if anyone carefully lays down other weapons where they could stay quiet if they were allowed, and someone then seizes that weapon and does any harm with it, then the following is right: that whoever did the harm should also (lacking in G) atone for the harm.

passages.text: [75, 1] si armature possessor inficiari (uoluerit) possit, illud malefactum nec sua uoluntate nec sua potestate nec suo consilio nec sua conscientia fuisse patratum, iustum secundum Deum censeo, armature possessorem esse innocentem,
passages.en: And whoever owns the weapon, let him clear himself, if he dares, [by the oath] that it [the crime] was never either his will, nor his intention, nor his counsel, nor his knowledge: then it is God's [that is, perfect] right that he stand clean.

passages.text: [75, 2] malefacti autem perpetratorem (facti) dampnum perpetratum corrigere secundum legis institutum.
passages.en: And let the other, who committed the [mis]deed, understand that he must atone for it as the law prescribes (the laws prescribe, G).

passages.text: [76] Si quis autem furtum in domum suam afferat, et ibi deprehensum fuerit, ipse autem conuictus fuerit, rectum est, ut accipiat hoc quod appetiit.
passages.en: (Of stolen goods. B) And if anyone brings a stolen thing home to his cottage and he is caught, it is right that [the owner] should have what he [tracking] went after.

passages.text: [76, 1] Et nisi sub seris marite locatum sit, immunis a crimine habeatur.
passages.en: And unless it was brought under the wife's lock (locks?, so A), let her stand clean.

passages.text: [76, 1<hi rend="italic">a</hi>] He autem sere sunt, quas marita obseruare debet: sera dispense et ciste et scrinii; quodsi sub aliqua harum locatum sit, non iudicetur innocens.
passages.en: On the other hand, she must keep watch over the following key (keys?), namely [look after] her storeroom (storeroom key, B) and her chest and her casket: if it has been brought under any one of these, then she is guilty.

passages.text: [76, 1<hi rend="italic">b</hi>] Nulla enim marita maritum prohibere potest, quin in sua propria domo locet quod uelit.
passages.en: But no wife may forbid her husband to put down (lay, B; bring in or unload?, A) in his cottage whatever he wants.

passages.text: [76, 2] Ante hoc quidem consuetudo erat, quod etiam infantulum qui iacebat in cunis, licet nondum unquam comedisset, auari pariter reum (esse) decernebant, ac si intellectum haberet.
passages.en: Until now it was the case that the child that lay in the cradle, even if it had [yet] never tasted food, that the greedy treated it as just as guilty as if it were capable of understanding.

passages.text: [76, 3] Sed amodo interdico hoc diligenter et multa similia, que sunt ualde odiosa Deo.
passages.en: But I forbid this earnestly henceforth, and many such things (very many things besides, B), which are most hateful to God.

passages.text: [77] Si quis propter formidolositatem fugiens, dominum uel socium destituerit siue nauali bello siue terrestri, . . . quicquid possidet cum propria uita; terra autem et mobilia cadant in iura et possessionem domini sui.
passages.en: (Of him who flees from his lord. B) And the man who through his cowardice flees from his lord or his companions (companion?), whether in the ship-army or in the land-army, let him lose all that he possesses and his own life; and let the lord take possession of his goods and of the land which he had previously given him.

passages.text: [77, 1] Qui si liberam terram habeat, cadat hec in ius regis.
passages.en: And if he holds land by [royal] charter, let it fall into the king's hand.

passages.text: [78] Qui autem in bello coram domino suo occidatur, siue in patria siue extra patriam: debita excercitualia condonentur; et heredes assumant terram et mobilia et diuidant inter se.
passages.en: (Of him who falls in his lord's presence. B) And the man who falls on campaign in the presence of his lord, whether in the land or away from the land: let the heriots be remitted [to his heirs]; and let the heirs take the land and movable goods and divide it very justly.

passages.text: [79] Et qui terram tutatus est testimonio comitatus, teneat eam immunem a calumpniis in die et post diem, utrum malit vendere seu dare cui libuerit.
passages.en: And whoever, with the witness of the shire, has defended an estate [in its obligations to the state] (since the former holder would not or could not [defend it], G), let him be allowed undisputed to sell and to give it away, in his lifetime and at his death, to whomever he most pleases.

passages.text: [U]olo etiam, ut omnis homo sua uenacione dignus sit tam in siluis quam in campis in suo proprio.
passages.en: (Of hunting. B) And I will that every man be entitled to his hunting in wood and field on his own land.

passages.text: [80, 1] Et dimittat meam uenacionem, ubicumque illam pacificatam esse uolo, super plenam forisfacturam.
passages.en: But let every man avoid my hunting, wherever I wish to have it protected [by forest-ban], on pain of the full fine.

passages.text: [82] (De pace domini regis et eius preceptis.) Precipio quoque, ut omnis homo pacem habeat placitum adeundo et a placito redeundo, nisi sit manifestus fur.
passages.en: And I will that every man be entitled to special peace-protection [on the way] to the court and from the court, unless he is an undeniable thief.

passages.text: [83] Quisquis autem hanc legem uiolauerit, quam rex nunc omnibus constituit, siue Danus siue Anglus, redempcionis sue reus sit erga regem.
passages.en: And whoever violates these statutes which the king has just now given to all people, whether he be Danish or (or, G) English, let him be liable for his wergild to the king.

passages.text: [83, 1] Quodsi secundo, bis persoluat censum sue redempcionis.
passages.en: And if he violates the [law] again, let him pay his wergild twice.

passages.text: [83, 2] Quodsi adeo audax si[t], ut illam tertio temeret, amittat quicquid possidet.
passages.en: And if he is then so bold that he violates it a third time, let him lose everything that he possesses.

passages.text: Nunc uero precor diligenter et nomine Dei iubeo hominem quemque, ut intimo corde supplicet Deo suo et sepe et frequenter satagat diligenter, quid sibi sit faciendum, et quid omittendum.
passages.en: Now I earnestly beg — and command in God's name — each and every person that he submit himself with his inmost heart to his Lord God and often and frequently consider very earnestly what he should do and what he should refrain from.

passages.text: Omnibus nobis uehementer expedit, ut Deum diligamus et Dei legem sequamur diuinisque doctoribus obediamus diligenter.
passages.en: There is great need for all of us that we love God and follow God's law(s?) and eagerly obey spiritual teachers.

passages.text: Ipsi enim nos debent producere ad iudicium, cum iudicauerit hominum quemque et ex precedentibus causis factis.
passages.en: For they shall lead us forth at the Judgment, when God will pass judgment on each person according to [his] earlier deeds.

passages.text: Felix ille pastor, qui tunc gregem suum in regnum et celestes delicias letus introducere meruit propter precedentia merita!
passages.en: And blessed will be the shepherd who may then joyfully lead the flock into God's kingdom and to heavenly bliss because of [their] earlier deeds.

passages.text: Bene erit etiam illi gregi, qui illum pastorem sequitur, qui se a diabolo abstrahit et adhereat Deo.
passages.en: And well for the flock that follows the shepherd who withdraws it from devils and wins it for God.

passages.text: Omnes itaque unanimi corde diligenter Deo [nostro] cum iusticia acceptemu[r] et acceptum seruicium faciamus et amodo semper proteg[a]mus nos a feruente incendio, quod feruet in inferno.
passages.en: So let us then all, with one heart, willingly and rightly be pleasing to our Lord God, and henceforth always eagerly shield ourselves from the hot fire that seethes in hell.

passages.text: Faciant eciam doctores et diuini precones ita [ut] iustum est et omnium hominum necessitas est: pre[dice]nt frequenter spiritualem utilitatem.
passages.en: And let teachers and spiritual heralds now also act as is right and to the benefit of all (likewise as, A) people, [namely] preach frequently [their] spiritual duty (duties?).

passages.text: Et omnis qui discrecionem habeat, attente illum audiat, diuinamque doctrinam quisque mente firmiter teneat, sibimet ad utilitatem.
passages.en: And let everyone who has understanding listen to them willingly, and let everyone hold spiritual teaching very firmly in memory, for his own benefit.

passages.text: Et semper hominum quisque in honorem sui Dei quod boni possit faciat uerbo et opere cum hylaritate; tunc erit nobis omnibus misericordia Dei paracior. . . . . . . . . .
passages.en: And let every person always, to the honour of his Lord God, joyfully do whatever good he can in word (and work, B) and deed; then God's mercy (God, B) will be the more ready for all of us.

passages.text: [32] Rex etiam edicit omnibus suis prepositis in omni loco per uniuersam gentem suam, quatinus abbatibus et omnibus ordinatis in omni seculari necessitate parcant, sicut melius potuerunt<ptr n="1" target="VIIIAtr_32.lnote.oe.1"/>, et, ueluti Dei et meam amiciciam diligant, adiuuent eorum ministros ad rectitudinem, ut et ipsi firmius in monasterio diuino officio et regulariter uiuere queant.
passages.en: And the king commands all his reeves in every place that you protect the abbots in all their worldly needs as best you can, and, as you wish to have God's friendship or mine, help their stewards everywhere to their rights, so that those [abbots] themselves may more often stay firmly in their minsters and live according to the rule.

passages.text: [33 <hi rend="italic">f</hi>.] Et, si quis usquam ordinatum iniuriet, quisque Dei amicus satagat, ut ei satisfaciat . . . .
passages.en: And if anyone in any way wrongs a man in holy orders or a foreigner, in property or in life, or binds or beats him or insults him in any way, then the king shall be to him in place of a kinsman and protector, unless he has another [protector].

passages.text: Illi<ptr n="d" target="ConsCn_II-84-4e.lnote.oe.d"/> autem ordinati faciant, ut sibi necessarium<ptr n="e" target="ConsCn_II-84-4e.lnote.oe.e"/> est: die noctuque inuocent Christum sepe et frequenter et pro cuncto Christiano populo intercedant diligenter.
passages.en: But let the men in orders do as is needful for them: let them call upon Christ day and night, often and frequently, and intercede diligently for the whole Christian people.

notes.en: cf. above p. 289*; Consil. I 6 seems to have been used here, not Cnut's original a second time

notes.de: swa him þearf is <hi rend="italic">las Quelle wie V Atr.</hi> 5
notes.en: swa him þearf is the source read, as V Atr. 5

passages.text: [43, 43, 1] Omnes quoque agamus, ut necessarium est nobis: intimo corde Deum omnipotentem adoremus et legem Dei custodiamus, ut melius poterimus.
passages.en: But let us do as we need to: let us take as our example what earlier secular councillors wisely decided, Æthelstan and Edmund and Edgar, who came last, how they honoured God and kept God's laws and paid God's dues as long as they lived.

passages.text: [44] Rectam Christianitatem attente honorificemus et omnem paganissimum<ptr n="1" target="VIIIAtr_44.lnote.oe.1"/> omnino contempnamus
passages.en: And let us eagerly honour true Christianity and utterly despise all heathenism.

passages.text: [44, 1] et ad unum regalem<ptr n="2" target="VIIIAtr_44-1.lnote.oe.2"/> dominum fide nos teneamus; amicorumque quisque fide recta alium amet et in rectitudine teneat<ptr n="3" target="VIIIAtr_44-1.lnote.oe.3"/> . . . .
passages.en: And let us loyally hold to one royal lord; and let each of [our] friends love the other with true loyalty and treat him rightly.

passages.text: In<ptr n="f" target="ConsCn_II-84-5.lnote.oe.f"/> eternum sit nomen Domini benedictum, cui laus et honor et gloria in secula seculorum!
passages.en: May the name of the Lord be blessed for ever, to whom be praise and honour and glory for ever and ever!

passages.text: Deus omnipotens omnibus nobis miser[e]at[ur<ptr n="4" target="ConsCn_II-84-6.lnote.oe.4"/>, sicut] libitum sit.
passages.en: May God almighty have mercy on us all, [as] may be his pleasure.

passages.text: De balatronibus.
passages.en: Of arsonists and of secret murders.

passages.text: Diximus de balatronibus et de furtiuis mortificatoribus, ut eorum iuramentum et iudiciale ferrum augeatur triplum, ut ponderet III libras, quod accusatus ipse ferat.
passages.en: We [the king and witan] have declared concerning arsonists and secret murders that their [clearing] oath be made three times heavier, or the ordeal iron be made larger so that it weighs 3 pounds; and let the accused man go to it himself [no representative to carry it].

passages.text: Accusator autem habeat electionem, utrum Dei iudicium malit, aque scilicet aut ferri.
passages.en: However, let the accuser have the choice: whether water ordeal or iron ordeal, whichever of the two he prefers [to demand that the other undergo].

passages.text: Si iuramentum illi deficit, qui si ceciderit, in decreto seniorum sit, qui ad illam urbem attinent, utrum uita ei concedatur, an morte puniatur.
passages.en: If he cannot bring forward such an oath, and he thus stands guilty, let it rest with the judgment of the most senior men who belong to that place of court [borough] whether he keeps his life or loses it.

passages.text: Anticipatio ubique, siue ultra unum comitatum siue ultra plures, XV nummi; et pro omni parua pecude semper pro solido nummus.
passages.en: [The reward for] seizing [stolen cattle] everywhere, whether in one shire [the same one where it was stolen] or across several, [is] 15 pence; and for each small beast [let the owner pay the rescuer] one penny per shilling [of value].

passages.text: De anticipacione sapientes consiliati sunt, ut per totam regionem simile iudicium teneatur, id est: pro homine XV nummi, pro equo tantumdem, siue ultra unum comitatum siue ultra plures, ne forte inbecillis et longe pro suo laboret necnon et nimium tribuat.
passages.en: Of [the reward for] recovery. Concerning the seizing [of stolen goods] the witan have decreed that the same law be kept over all England (the whole land, B, Cons.): namely [let the owner pay the rescuer] 15 pence for [each recovered] slave, and the same for a horse, whether [it had to be pursued] across one shire or across several, lest a man without means should toil far for his own [property] and also pay too much.

passages.text: Olim statutum fuit, ut iuxta numerum comitatuum anticipacio daretur.
passages.en: Formerly [indeed] it held that (the [reward for] seizure was paid according to the number of shires [between the theft and the capture].

passages.text: Uetus rectum quidem est, ut pro omni furata pecunia secundum precium ipsius anticipacio detur, id est pro solido nummus, cuiuscunque generis pecunia sit, si a manibus furis erepta sit;
passages.en: But true law is that — lacking in B) seizure-money be paid for every stolen beast according to its (value — lacking in B), namely [1] penny for every shilling, of whatever kind the beast may be, if [that is] it is snatched from the thief's hand.

passages.text: sin autem in repostaculo reperta, tunc poterit census anticipacionis moderacior esse, eo quod minori periculo nacta sit.
passages.en: If, on the other hand, it is found elsewhere, in hiding, then the rescue-fee may be lighter, because it was obtained at less risk.

passages.text: <ptr n="*" target="Hu_Inscr.lnote.oe.star"/><ptr n="1" target="Hu_Inscr.lnote.oe.1-2"/>Hec est consiliatio<ptr n="2" target="Hu_Inscr.lnote.oe.2-2"/>, quomodo centenarii<ptr n="3" target="Hu_Inscr.lnote.oe.3"/> conuentus obseruari debet.
passages.en: This is the ordinance on how the hundred[-court] is to be held.

Hr has the heading De hundredis

passages.text: Primum quidem quod semper<ptr n="4" target="Hu_1.lnote.oe.4"/> circa IIII septimanas congregentur<ptr n="5" target="Hu_1.lnote.oe.5"/>, et quisque<ptr n="6" target="Hu_1.lnote.oe.6"/> alii rectum faciat.
passages.en: First, that they [the inhabitants of the hundred] assemble every four weeks, and that everyone do [legal] right to the other.

passages.text: Quodsi necessitas instet, primum nuncietur concionatori centenarii, qui deinde decimacionariis (id est singulis qui presunt decimacionibus); omnesque proficiscantur, quoadusque<ptr n="7" target="Hu_2.lnote.oe.7-2"/> ducatu Dei perueniant quo cupiunt; furi quidem quod rectum est faciant, secundum quod ante ab Eadmundo rege institutum est.
passages.en: (That the men pursue the thieves in a riding party. B) If there is urgent need, let it be announced to the hundred-man, and he then to the tithing-men; and they are all to go out wherever God shows them that they may reach [the goal]; [let] the thief's lawful [punishment] be carried out on him, as was previously (King, Qu., Con.) Edmund's ordinance.

passages.text: Possessori autem sue rei precium reddatur de rebus, si forte res ipsa furto ablata periit; residuum uero in duo diuidatur: et quidem dimidium cadat in ius et possessionem tocius centenarii, dimidium uero in ius domini — preter homines (uel<ptr n="8" target="Hu_2-1.lnote.oe.8"/> familiam), qui soli domino contingant.
passages.en: And let the compensation-money [from the thief's goods] be paid to the owner of the [stolen] cattle; and let the rest be divided in two [halves]: half to the hundred, half to the lord [of the thief] — except for the [thief's] dependants; namely, let the lord receive these dependants [all].

passages.text: Qui autem hoc neglexerint et iudicium centenarii repudiauerint, iterum summonitus idem det primo centenario XXX d., secundo uero LX, quod quidem dimidium centenario, dimidium domino uere contingat.
passages.en: And anyone who neglects this and [so] rejects the decision of the hundred — and [if] the same is afterwards proved against him —, let him pay the hundred 30 pence, and the second time 60 pence, half to the hundred, half to [his] lord.

passages.text: Quodsi tercio obtigerit, det dimidiam libram; si autem quarto, amittat omnia que possidet; ipse autem sit exlex, nisi<ptr n="9" target="Hu_3-1.lnote.oe.9"/> rex patriam ei indulgeat.
passages.en: If he does it a third time, let him pay half a pound; the fourth time let him lose everything he has and be outlawed, unless the king permits him [to remain in] the homeland.

notes.en: n. rex in the margin Hr

passages.text: Diximus etiam de ignoto pecore, ne quis illud habeat absque<ptr n="10" target="Hu_4.lnote.oe.10"/> testimonio concionatoris uel decimationarii, et hic<ptr n="10a" target="Hu_4.lnote.oe.10a"/> sit fidelissimus.
passages.en: And we determined concerning cattle of unknown [origin] that no one keep [such], unless he has the witness(es?) [for its acquisition] of the hundred-man or of the tithing-man, and that this man be thoroughly trustworthy.

passages.text: Absque<ptr n="11" target="Hu_4-1.lnote.oe.11"/> uero utro (id<ptr n="12" target="Hu_4-1.lnote.oe.12"/> est alterius eorum testimonio) nulla ei attestacio indulgeatur (id<ptr n="12" target="Hu_4-1.lnote.oe.12"/> est: liceat ei trahere aliquem ad tutelam, quod ab eo habuit).
passages.en: And unless he has one of these, let him be refused permission to vouch to warranty.

notes.de: Si a. ue. sit <hi rend="italic">statt</hi> A. u. ut. <hi rend="italic">Hk</hi>
notes.en: Si a. ue. sit instead of A. u. ut. Hk

passages.text: Item diximus, quod, si persone<ptr n="13" target="Hu_5.lnote.oe.13"/> unius centenarii sequantur uestigia (furati<ptr n="14" target="Hu_5.lnote.oe.14"/> animalis) in territorium alterius centenarii, nuncietur concionatori (illius<ptr n="12" target="Hu_5.lnote.oe.12"/> scilicet, quo iam peruenerunt), qui simul cum (illis<ptr n="15" target="Hu_5.lnote.oe.15"/>) proficiscatur.
passages.en: We also determined: if a hundred leads the track for him [the man tracing lost property] into another hundred, that it be reported to the head of the latter hundred, and that he then go along there [in the search].

notes.de: <hi rend="italic">verbessert aus</hi> illo <hi rend="italic">Hk; fehlt</hi> [<hi rend="italic">ursprünglicher?</hi>] <hi rend="italic">Hr</hi>
notes.en: corrected from illo Hk; lacking [more original?] in Hr

passages.text: Quod si recuset, det regi XXX solidos.
passages.en: If he neglects it, let him pay the king 30 shillings.

passages.text: Si quis rectitudinem deuitans effugiat, soluat illud simpliciter<ptr n="1" target="Hu_6.lnote.oe.1-2"/> (quod<ptr n="2" target="Hu_6.lnote.oe.2"/> petitur per illam calumpniam, propter quam effugit ille) qui eum (effugere<ptr n="3" target="Hu_6.lnote.oe.3"/>) ad illud iacture seruauit.
passages.en: If anyone avoids fulfilling his legal obligation by absconding, let whoever kept him for this doing of harm pay the single compensation.

passages.text: Qui si calumpnietur, quod eum effugere fecerit, purget se secundum legem patrie.
passages.en: And if this man is accused of having let him go, let him clear himself as is valid in the [law of the] land.

passages.text: In centenariis necnon et in<ptr n="4" target="Hu_7.lnote.oe.4"/> aliis placitis uolumus, ut puplica rectitudo (teneatur<ptr n="2" target="Hu_7.lnote.oe.2"/> uel) decernatur<ptr n="5" target="Hu_7.lnote.oe.5"/> in omni causa (inter<ptr n="3" target="Hu_7.lnote.oe.3"/> uirum et uirum), et ut inducietur<ptr n="6" target="Hu_7.lnote.oe.6"/>, donec perficiatur (rectitudo<ptr n="3" target="Hu_7.lnote.oe.3"/>).
passages.en: In the hundred as in any other court we will that folk-right be ordered in every suit, and a term be set for when the [judgment] is to be fulfilled.

passages.text: Qui illas inducias fregerit (quas<ptr n="2" target="Hu_7-1.lnote.oe.2"/> auctoritas totius centuriatus statuit), nisi sit propter edictum domini (sui<ptr n="2" target="Hu_7-1.lnote.oe.2"/>), emendet hoc XXX sol., et statuto termino (alio<ptr n="3" target="Hu_7-1.lnote.oe.3"/>) perficiat quod prius deberet.
passages.en: And whoever breaks this term — unless it is because of a summons by [his] lord —, let him pay 30 shillings and perform on the [newly] appointed day what he should have done before.

passages.text: Nola bouis, collarium canis (Anglice<ptr n="7" target="Hu_8.lnote.oe.7"/> dicitur ‘hundes hoppe’, quasi canis circularium, quia hóp: circulus), tuba cornea<ptr n="8" target="Hu_8.lnote.oe.8"/>: horum trium unumquodque ualet<ptr n="9" target="Hu_8.lnote.oe.9"/> unum<ptr n="10" target="Hu_8.lnote.oe.10"/> sol.; et<ptr n="4" target="Hu_8.lnote.oe.4"/> uniuscuiusque<ptr n="11" target="Hu_8.lnote.oe.11"/> modus<ptr n="12" target="Hu_8.lnote.oe.12"/> computatus [melda<ptr n="13" target="Hu_8.lnote.oe.13"/>].<ptr n="*" target="Hu_8.lnote.oe.star"/>
passages.en: An ox's bell, a dog's collar, a blowing-horn: each of these three is worth 1 shilling; and each is reckoned as an informer.

Computatus propter dampnum [pro dampno <hi rend="italic">Cb</hi>], quod ex hiis possit fortasse [quod de nola potest c. <hi rend="italic">Hk</hi>] contingere, uel propter dedecus <hi rend="italic">fügt zu Hk und, nach Überspringung der</hi> Comput. <hi rend="italic">endenden Zeile, Cb.</hi>

Hk] contingere, uel propter dedecus added by Hk and, after skipping the line ending in Comput., by Cb.

passages.text: Ferrum<ptr n="14" target="Hu_9.lnote.oe.14"/> triplicis Dei iudicii ponderet III<ptr n="15" target="Hu_9.lnote.oe.15"/> libras.
passages.en: The iron which belongs to the threefold ordeal is to weigh 3 pounds.
